To date, 10 cases have been reported in 271 patients (3.6%).Avascular necrosis is a less common adverse effect (10% to 20%) associated with corticosteroids (Answer C is incorrect). No patients with ITP have developed myelodysplastic syndrome after romiplostim therapy (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 62-year-old man has microscopic hematuria found on screening urinalysis for his diabetes. His complete blood cell count reveals a platelet count of 23,000/ mm3, a hemoglobin concentration of 14.,5 g/dL, and a normal peripheral blood smear. He has a history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and coronary artery disease. His drugs include aspirin, insulin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. He is RhD,positive. Based on a diagnosis of ITP, which one of the following is the most appropriate initial therapy for this patient?
options: B. Intravenous immune globulin and dexamethasone.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. All the answers are reasonable choices for the management of newly diagnosed ITP. The response rate after intravenous anti-D immune globulin is similar to corticosteroids;however, it is less likely to cause hyperglycemia and hypertension, and it may provide a sustained response (Answer D is correct). The patient is Rh (D) positive, has no history of splenectomy, and has hemoglobin above 10 g/dL, making him an appropriate candidate for intravenous anti-D immune globulin. Dexamethasone is reported in clinical trials to be well tolerated, even among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. However, patients with uncontrolled diabetes and hypertension were excluded from these trials, and in clinical practice, it has been observed to worsen blood glucose and blood pressure control (Answer A is incorrect). The combination of dexamethasone and immune globulin is appropriate as emergency therapy for patients with clinically significant bleeding; however, this patient has microscopic hematuria and is asymptomatic (Answer B is incorrect). Rituximab combined with dexamethasone is effective as salvage therapy after corticosteroids have failed. Based on the additional risk of toxicity and expense with rituximab, it is more appropriate to delay treatment with rituximab until patients have relapsed after initial corticosteroid therapy (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A patient has persistent ITP with a platelet count of 26,000/mm3 despite corticosteroid therapy. He is referred to a surgeon for splenectomy but is determined not to undergo surgery. His comorbidities include type 2 diabetes mellitus, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and chronic renal insufficiency. His SCr is 1.8 mg/dL, and he has hormal liver function tests. Which one of the following is the most appropriate therapy for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. About 40% to 60% of patients with ITP attain a platelet count above 50,000/mm3 after rituximab administration, and 28% to 46% achieve platelet counts above 150,000/ mm3.Rituximab is least likely to cause additional toxicity given the patient's comorbidities(Answer B is correct). Cyclosporine may be effective therapy; however, it is nephrotoxic and may worsen his peripheral neuropathy and glucose control (Answer A is incorrect).Intravenous immune globulin is not appropriate monotherapy for chronic ITP because the effects are transient, and the duration of benefit becomes progressively shorter with continued administration (Answer C is incorrect). The dose-limiting adverse effect for vincristine is neuropathy, which will likely worsen the patient's peripheral neuropathy(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 68-year-old man with chronic ITP has been refractory to treatment with corticosteroids; he developed recurrent thrombocytopenia after a splenectomy. He has a history of hepatitis B. His platelet count is 22,000/mm3, and he has been having frequent epistaxis. His alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is 89 IU/L, aspartate aminotransferase(AST) is 175 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is 153 IU/L, and SCr is 1 mg/ dL.Which one of the following is the most appropriate therapy for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. About 40% of patients with ITP and a prior splenectomy achieve a durable response pfiter romiplostim. Romiplostim has no contraindications for liver dysfunction or a history of hepatitis, so it is the most appropriate agent for the patient (Answer C is correct). Azathioprine can cause hepatotoxicity with chronic use; it should be avoided in this patient (Answer A is incorrect). Eltrombopag is hepatically metabolized and has a poxed warning for hepatotoxicity. A dose reduction to 25 mg daily is recommended in patients with moderate to severe liver dysfunction. Eltrombopag could be prescribed for his patient; however, romiplostim is a safer alternative (Answer B is incorrect). Among HBsAgnegative/ anti-HBc positive lymphoma patients treated with rituximab,Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone, 25% developed hepatitis B virus reactivation compared with 0% receiving the same drugs without rituximab. Close monitoring for at least 6 months after rituximab therapy is required. If an effective plternative to rituximab is available, that agent should be used (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the most significant limitation in clinical trials with romiplostim for ITP?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The most significant limitation to clinical trials with romiplostim is the lack of a niform, active control arm (Answer A is correct). Clinical trials of romiplostim in patients with ITP have used either a placebo as the control arm or an open-label,investigator-selected, standard of care as the control arm. Some patients received medical management with watchful waiting alone. Without a uniform control arm, it is difficult to discern whether romiplostim is superior to any single agent. It is also unclear whether some of the patients received a standard of care to which they had previously been exposed. Two phase III, randomized, controlled trials have been conducted with pomiplostim; therefore, study design for this drug is actually a strength of the clinical tals compared with other therapies for ITP (Answer B is incorrect). The primary end point of clinical trials with romiplostim has been improvement in platelet counts, nol prevention of clinically significant bleeding, which is the goal of therapy in patients with ITP (Answer C is incorrect). The rate of clinically significant bleeding is low in patients with ITP, and clinicians often initiate rescue therapy before patients develop clinically significant bleeding, making this is a difficult, idealistic clinical trial end point. Although this is an important critique of the studies, it is not the most significant limitation. The ollow-up duration is a limitation to trials of romiplostim in patients with ITP because patients received therapy for a maximum of I year. Patients who respond to romiplostim will need to continue therapy indefinitely to sustain a platelet response. However, this Answer is incorrect because, compared with other therapies, this is a long duration for a clinical trial in ITP (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 57-year-old woman has chronic ITP refractory to splenectomy and rituximab. She also has osteoporosis, hyperlipidemia, pancreatitis, and menopausal hot flashes. Her current drugs include prednisone, omega- 3-acid ethyl esters, pravastatin, alendronate,calcium, and vitamin D. Her platelet count is 17,000/mm3, ALT is 34 IU/L, AST is 23 IU/L, ALP is 89 IU/L, and SCr is 0.6 mg/dL. She is expressing frustration with the cost of all of her drugs. Which one of the following is the most appropriate therapy for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The patient has no contraindications to cyclophosphamide, and a sustained response may be seen in up to one-half of patients, making cyclophosphamide the best answer (Answer D is correct). Danazol is an androgen that may cause hot flashes and elevations in LDH and may worsen the patient's menopausal symptoms and lipid control (Answer A incorrect). Azathioprine may cause pancreatitis; it should be avoided if possible because of the patient's history of pancreatitis (Answer B is incorrect). Eltrombopag is the most expensive drug of these options, with an average whole sale price of 3960$ for a 30-day supply. Because cost is a concern for this patient,it is not the best option(answer c is incorrect).

questions.question: A 61-year-old man with chronic ITP has been off all therapies after splenectomy,maintaining platelet counts of 20,000-40,000/mm3 without clinically significant bleeding. He recently received a diagnosis of prostate cancer; he is scheduled to undergo prostatectomy in 3 weeks. His platelet count is currently 27,000/ mm3, but the surgeon wants it to be above 80,000/mm3 for the surgery. Which one of the following therapies is most appropriate for this patient?
options: B. Intravenous immune globulin once daily for 2 days immediately before surgery.
C. Rituximab once weekly for 4 weeks starting today and one dose immediately before surgery.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Intravenous immune globulin is recommended to provide a rapid increase in platelet counts before a surgical procedure. About 80% of patients have a rapid increase in platelet count within 24 hours, making this is the most reliable method to increase his platelet count (Answer B is correct). Danazol is effective therapy for chronic ITP;owever, it typically takes 3-6 months to see a response in platelet counts. An androgerl s contraindicated in a patient with prostate cancer; therefore, this is a less correct option Answer A is incorrect). The median time to response with rituximab is 4-6 weeks,Rituximab should not be used to rapidly raise platelet counts prior to a surgical procedure. This patient's surgery is scheduled to take place in 3 weeks and it unlikely the patient would have responded to rituximab before surgery (Answer C is incorrect).Eltrombopag could be an option to increase his platelet count before a surgical procedure in 3 weeks because most patients who do respond will respond within 2 weeks and 60% to 80% of patients achieve platelet counts above 50,000/mm3; however;immune globulin remains the standard of care for increasing platelet counts prior to a surgical procedure. (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 54-year-old man was recently admitted to the hospital for acute myocardial infarction. He has a history of chronic ITP and has been observed off therapy after splenectomy with platelet counts ranging from 20,000/mm3 to 30,000/mm3 without clinically significant bleeding. Before splenectomy, he received rituximab with no response. He was given a dose of immune globulin before coronary bypass surgery, and his platelet count increased to 103,000/mm3; however, it has declined during the past 2 weeks and is currently 54,000/mm3. He is being discharged on clopidogrel, aspirin,metoprolol, enalapril, and simvastatin 40 mgdaily. Which one of the following therapies is most appropriate to manage ITP in this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The administration of aspirin and clopidogrel increases the patient's risk of bleeding; it is recommended to keep his platelet counts above 40,000-50,000/mm3. His platelet Counts are expected to return to his previous baseline of 20,000-30,000/mm3 before intravenous immune globulin is administered. Eltrombopag is effective in 60% of patients with chronic ITP, and the patient has no contraindications to therapy. It is likely to raise his platelet counts within 2 weeks if it is effective for him and is the most appropriate answer (Answer D is correct). Danazol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor that increases the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis when coadministered with simvastatin,Danazol commonly causes fluid retention and may put him at increased risk of developing congestive heart failure. The full response to danazol may take 3-6 months,and he would likely need additional therapy to manage his ITP in the interim if this dnug were selected (Answer A is incorrect). Vincristine is also a CYP3A4 inhibitor that increases the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis when coadministered with simvastatin. Vincristine is unlikely to provide a sustained response off therapy and will likely cause peripheral neuropathy with continued administration (Answer B is incorrect). Cyclosporine also is a CYP3A4 inhibitor that produces a 6- to 8-fold increase in simvastatin exposure when administered concomitantly; increasing the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis (Answer C is incorrect). Low doses of simvastatin or an alternative agent should be considered in the absence of other alternatives to cyclosporine for the treatment of ITP.

questions.question: A 24-year-old woman with chronic ITP has been receiving romiplostim for the past 6 weeks. She completed the ITP-Patient Assessment Questionnaire in the waiting room before her clinic appointment with you. Which one of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of her health-related quality of life (HRQoL) based on the results below?
options: A. Improvement in bother, social activity, and reproductive health.
B. Improvement in symptoms, fatigue, bother, activity, psychological health, social activity, reproductive health, and overall QoL.
C. Improvement in fatigue, bother, activity, social activity, and reproductive health.
D. Decline in work and fear.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The range for clinically meaningful change is 8-12 points for symptoms, bother,psychological health, fear, social activity, work, reproductive health, and overall QoL of the ITP-Patient Assessment Questionnaire (ITP-PAQ). The range for clinically meaningful change is 10-15 points for fatigue and activity. Improvements in bothel(+12), social activity (+14),and reproductive health (+13)are significant and consisten with observations in romiplostim clinical trials (Answer A is correct). Answer B is incorrect because symptoms (+5), fatigue (+8), activity (+9), psychological health (+9)and overall QoL (+3) did not increase by the amount considered a meaningful change Answer C is incorrect because fatigue (+8) and activity (+9) did not increase by the amount considered a meaningful change. Answer D is incorrect because the decreases observed in work and fear is not considered a meaningful change.

questions.question: A 41-year-old man presents with fatigue and severe abdominal pain for the past 3 weeks. His hemoglobin is 5.7 g/dL, platelet count is 233,000/mm3, and neutrophil count is 3800/mm3. His total bilirubin is 2.8 mg/ dL, direct bilirubin is 0.2 mg/dL, reticulocyte count is 6.8%, and LDH is 3800 IU/L. Abdominal ultrasonography reveals a superior mesenteric venous thrombosis. Peripheral blood flow cytometry reveals a PNH type III clone affecting 55% of his erythrocytes. He is given a diagnosis of classic PNH. He has a matched related donor and meets eligibility criteria for an allogeneic HSCT. Which one of the following therapies is most appropriate for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The patient has classic PNH with evidence of clinically significant hemolysis,thrombosis, and symptoms related to PNH. Eculizumab reduces hemolysis, eliminates transfusions in one-half of patients on therapy, and improves quality of life. The patient has thrombosis and therefore requires warfarin (Answer A is correct). Allogeneic HSCT should be reserved for patients with classic PNH that does not respond to eculizumab(Answer B is incorrect). Warfarin is indicated for patients with PNH and thrombosis;however, it does not mitigate other manifestations of PNH. Prednisone should not be used to manage PNH chronically; the patient would derive more benefit from eculizumab than prednisone (Answer C is incorrect). Patients with classic PNH are unlikely to benefit from immunosuppressive therapy, therefore, cyclosporine and antithymocyte globulin is not the best option (Answer Dis incorrect).

questions.question: A 24-year-old woman with a known history of classic PNH presents with significant fatigue and shortness of breath. Laboratory studies reveal her hemoglobin to be 6.3 g/dL,platelet count 484,000/mm3, neutrophil count 4100/mm3, total bilirubin 2.2 mg/dL,direct bilirubin 0.3 mg/dL, ferritin 83 ng/mL (normal 13-150 ng/mL), reticulocyte count 4.5%, and LDH 2900 IU/L. She has no history of thrombosis. Peripheral blood flow cytometry reveals a PNH type IlI clone affecting 70% of her erythrocytes, increased from her last measurement of 20% of erythrocytes. Her physician decides to initiate therapy with eculizumab. Which one of the following is most important for the patient to receive before eculizumab is initiated?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Treatment with eculizumab increases the risk of meningococcal sepsis, and all patients should be vaccinated with the meningococcal polysaccharide vaccine 2 weeks before initiating therapy. Although all four answers may be beneficial for the patient,prevention of meningococcal sepsis is the most critical intervention before initiating eculizumab (Answer D is correct). Iron deficiency is not uncommon in patients with PNH; however, the patient does not have evidence of iron deficiency based on her ferritin. She should be monitored for the development of iron deficiency, but iron replacement is not indicated at this time (Answer A is incorrect). All patients with PNH should receive folate supplementation to support erythropoiesis; however, it may be delayed until after vaccination (Answer B is incorrect). Because PNH is considered a chronic disease, influenza vaccination is a prudent intervention. However, the risks associated with meningococcal sepsis are higher; therefore, the meningococcal polysaccharide vaccine should be administered first (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A 37-year-old woman with a known history of classic PNH began taking eculizumab 6 months ago and had considerable improvement in her fatigue, with an increase in her hemoglobin and reduction in laboratory studies assessing hemolysis. She is currently receiving eculizumab 900 mg every 14 days, ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times/day, and folic acid 5 mg/day. Three days ago, she presented with significant fatigue, shortness of breath, productive cough, chills, and nasal congestion. She was prescribed levofloxacin 750 mg/day for 10 days. Laboratory studies today reveal her hemoglobin to be 7.1 g/dL,platelet count 271,000/mm3, neutrophil count 9900/mm3, total bilirubin 3.6 mg/ dL,direct bilirubin 0.3 mg/dL, ferritin 115 ng/mL, reticulocyte count 3.3%, and LDH 8900 IU/L. She has no history of thrombosis. Peripheral blood flow cytometry reveals a PNH type III clone affecting 60%0f her erythrocytes, which is increased from her baseline measurement of 40% when she began taking eculizumab. Which one of the following approaches is most appropriate at this time for this patient?
options: A. Change eculizumab to 900 mg once every 12 days.
B. Discontinue eculizumab and proceed to an allogeneic HSCT.
C. Add prednisone 40 mg once daily for 10 days.
D. Add danazol 200 mg two times/day for 10 days.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The patient has a history of a recent infection, and patients with PNH may develop exacerbations of hemolysis and PNH symptoms during an infection. The patient's increase in hemolysis is not an indication she is failing the current treatment regimen;rather, it is a reflection of an acute exacerbation associated with infection. If significant hemolysis is present, patients may be given a short pulse of corticosteroids to suppress hemolysis ( Answer C is correct) . The increase in PNH erythrocytes is expected during treatment with eculizumab because it prevents the destruction of PNH erythrocytes. About 2% of patients have breakthrough hemolysis at the end of the dosing interval with eculizumab and may benefit from a 12-day dosing interval; however, the Increase in hemolysis is more likely related to her recent infection, so this is not the best Option (Answer A is incorrect). Allogeneic HSCT should not be considered unless the patient has persistent hemolysis and PNH symptoms after resolution of her infection(Answer B is incorrect). Danazol often takes weeks to months to take effect; therefore, it is unlikely to be beneficial during an acute exacerbation of hemolysis (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 57-year-old man presents with fatigue and petechiae. His hemoglobin is 7.3 g/dL,platelet count is 12,000/ mm3, and neutrophil count is 470/mm3. His total bilirubin is 1.4 mg/dL, direct bilirubin is 0.3 mg/dL, reticulocyte count is 0.2%, and LDH is 380IU/L. Peripheral blood flow cytometry reveals a PNH type II clone affecting 10% of his erythrocytes. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy reveal a hypocellular marrow. He has a Diagnosis of severe aplastic anemia and PNH-subclinical. He was adopted and has no known siblings. He does meet eligibility criteria for a matched unrelated donor allogeneic HSCT. Which one of the following therapies is most appropriate for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The patient has PNH with an underlying bone marrow disorder; therefore, his therapy Bhould be directed at the underlying bone marrow disorder, aplastic anemia. The patienl is older than 40 years and does not have a matched related donor; therefore, the most appropriate treatment for him is immunosuppression with cyclosporine and antithymocyte globulin (Answer D is correct). Prednisone alone is not as efficacious as immunosuppression with cyclosporine and antithymocyte globulin (Answer A is incorrect). The patient does not have significant hemolysis and is unlikely to benefit from eculizumab (Answer B is incorrect). Patients older than 40 years undergoing allogeneic HSCT with a matched unrelated donor experience increased treatment related mortality compared with younger patients with a matched related donor; therefore, the correct approach is a trial of immunosuppressive therapy before consideration of allogeneic HSCT (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A 32-year-old woman presents with right lower extremity pain and swelling.Doppler ultrasonography of her leg reveals an acute deep venous thrombosis. Her laboratory results are as follows: hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, platelet count 457,000/mm3 neutrophil count 4700/ mm3, total bilirubin 1.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL,reticulocyte count 3.3%, and LDH 890 IU/L. Peripheral blood flow cytometry reveals a PNH type III clone affecting 40% of her erythrocytes. She receives a diagnosis of classic PNH. Which one of the following therapies is most appropriate for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The patient has classic PNH with evidence of thrombosis. Thrombosis is the leading cause of death in patients with PNH and is an indication for treatment of PNH. Patients should receive both anticoagulation and appropriate treatment of PNH; the patient has classic PNH, so she should receive eculizumab and warfarin (Answer B is correct).Treatment with eculizumab may decrease the risk of recurrent thrombosis in PNH;however, until further data are available, patients should be anticoagulated indefinitely unless the PNH is cured. Patients receiving eculizumab should continue on warfarin unless they have contraindications to therapy. Adding aspirin to eculizumab is inappropriate therapy because this has not been shown effective in preventing recurrent thrombosis in patients with PNH (Answer A is incorrect). The patient has no PNH symptoms other than those related to her deep venous thrombosis. Thrombosis is associated with increased mortality in PNH and is an indication to treat classic PNH even if patients do not have significant hemolysis; therefore, treatment with warfarin alone is inappropriate (Answer C is incorrect). There are insufficient data to support sustained use of prednisone for treatment of classic PNH. The patient has evidence of hemolysis; however, she does not require transfusions because her hemoglobin is above 8 g/dL, so there is no indication to use prednisone at this time (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A patient receiving eltrombopag is admitted to the hospital and given a diagnosis of myelofibrosis. To which one of the following is it most important to report this adverse event?
options: A. A Risk Evaluation and Management Strategy program
C. An institutional adverse event reporting system.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. All the answers are appropriate actions after the development of a significant adverse drug event related to a new drug. One of the requirements of the Risk Evaluation and Management Strategy (REMs) program for a thrombopoietin agonist is the reporting of myeloid neoplasms. Failure to comply with this reporting may jeopardize an institution's ability to prescribe and distribute eltrombopag to patients; therefore, this is the best answer (Answer A is correct). Reporting to the FDA by a Med Watch form is appropriate but optional for health care professionals (Answer B is incorrect). Reporting this adverse event to an institutional adverse event reporting system may be helpful for tracking institutional adverse events; however, reporting adverse events is likely to be elective(Answer C is incorrect). Reporting this adverse event to the manufacturer will be done using the REMs program; there is no need to report it directly to the manufacturer(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A pharmacy resident at a tertiary referral center for hematologic disorders wants to do a residency project that assesses HRQoL in patients with hematologic malignancies.She is planning to administer an HRQoL survey to patients during her residency. Which one of the following patient populations would provide the most meaningful contribution to the literature and could accrue a reasonable sample size in 1 year?
options: A. Patients receiving eculizumab for PNH.
B. Patients receiving splenectomy for ITP.
C. Patients receiving an allogeneic HSCT for PNH.
D. Patients receiving eltrombopag for ITP.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Health-related quality of life has not been assessed in patients undergoing splenectomy for ITP (Answer B is correct). Because splenectomy is currently the prefered second.-line treatment for ITP, patient accrual to this study design would be most feasible during a l-year residency and would provide a meaningful contribution to the literature.Eculizumab for ITP already has QoL information that shows significant benefit with this agent. A residency project in this area would be a less meaningful contribution to the literature than other areas (Answer A is incorrect). No data exist for HRQoL in patients with PNH undergoing allogeneic HSCT, critical information for a procedure that has both a high cure rate and a high morbidity rate. Because PNH is rare, with two cases per I million people in the United States, a single institution is unlikely to accrue sufficient patients to provide meaningful information (Answer C is incorrect). Health-related quality of life has previously been reported in patients receiving eltrombopag for ITP Because of both prior knowledge and the smaller population receiving this intervention for ITP, this answer is incorrect (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 62-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma presents with jaundice, nausea, and a 6.4-kg (14 Ib) weight loss in the past month. She is very fatigued and has been unable to work at her job as an administrative assistant. She spends about 80% of her time in bed or in a recliner. Except for a total bilirubin of 5.6 mg/dL, her organ function and laboratory values are within normal limits. Her medical history is significant only for hypertension. Her drugs include lisinopril, aspirin, and furosemide. Which one of the following treatments is the best first-line therapy for this patient?
options: D. Enrollment in a clinical trial.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. This patient has metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (PS) of 3, as evidenced by her inability to perform usual daily activities. Gemcitabine monotherapy is the best option for this patient because it improves quality of life (QoL) and prolongs life in patients with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma (Answer B is correct). Surgery with total pancreatectomy is not a good option because it is not curative given that she has metastatic disease(Answer A is incorrect). Surgery may be used as palliative therapy in some patients, but it is also not an ideal choice because the risks associated with surgery likely outweigh any benefits. Gemcitabine and erlotinib are beneficial only in patients with a good PS(Answer C is incorrect). Clinical trials are usually available only to patients with a good PS (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group 0-2) and are not considered first-line therapy because it is unknown whether their QoL benefits are similar to treatment with gemcitabine (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 54-year-old woman has received a diagnosis of localized pancreatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head. All diagnostic scans for metastatic disease are negative. She is otherwise healthy and is scheduled for a complete resection of the tumor. Which one of the following approaches is best to treat this patient after her resection?
options: A. Gemcitabine and best supportive care (BSC).
C. Gemcitabine followed by fluorouracil-based chemoradiation therapy.
D. Fluorouracil followed by gemcitabine-based chemoradiation therapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. This patient has resectable disease; however, 80% of patients with resectable disease have disease recurrence after surgery. Radiation and/or chemotherapy are used in most situations, and this combination increases local control and overall survival (OS).Toxicities may be encountered, but this patient is healthy and likely to tolerate the treatment. Aggressive therapy is preferable to give her the best outcome. The study looking at fluorouracil and gemcitabine before and after chemoradiation showed a trend toward significance with increasing OS in patients with tumors of the head of the pancreas. Gemcitabine followed by fluorouracil-based radiation therapy is best because it is the most aggressive of the therapies (Answer C is correct). Fluorouracil with Concurrent radiation alone has generally been considered the standard of care, but adding gemcitabine before the therapy would be better in this patient because she has a tumor of the pancreatic head (Answer B is incorrect). Gemcitabine after fluorouracil-based radiation has not been studied (Answer D is incorrect). Radiation increases local disease control, so gemcitabine monotherapy with supportive care is not the best option (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 64-65 pertain to the following case. M.N. is a 78-year-old man with a diagnosis of locoregionally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He is otherwise in good health and has had no debilitating symptoms of the disease so far. He wants to be as aggressive as possible with his treatment. In addition to gemcitabine therapy, which one of the following is the best treatment option for M.N.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. This patient has unresectable disease, is fairly healthy, and wishes to undergo aggressive lreatment. Gemcitabine and erlotinib (Answer B is correct) is the only combination therapy that increases OS over gemcitabine with supportive care alone (Answer A is Incorrect). Chemoradiation (Answer C is incorrect) is not a good option in a patient who has unresectable disease because chemoradiation is not usually used unless there ig chance that the disease could become surgically resectable. Irinotecan (Answer D is incorrect) has not shown an advantage over gemcitabine alone.

questions.question: Questions 64-65 pertain to the following case. M.N. is a 78-year-old man with a diagnosis of locoregionally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma... M.N. experiences a recurrence 3 months after finishing his treatment. He tolerated his previous treatment well, and he is dedicated to remaining as aggressive as possible with his treatment. His quality of life (QoL) is still good, and he plays nine holes of golf at least once a week. He is not interested in participating in a clinical trial. Laboratory values include bilirubin 2.1 mg/dL and serum creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. All other values are Within normal limits. He wants to start therapy today or tomorrow so that he can keep his vacation plans. Which one of the following is the best treatment option for M.N.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The patient has a good PS, and surgery is not an option because he has unresectable disease, so chemotherapy is a good option for him. The combination of oxaliplatin,fluorouracil, and leucovorin improves progression-free survival and OS in second-line Studies (Answer A is correct). Fixed-dose-rate gemcitabine is not appropriate because he received gemcitabine 3 months ago and relapsed (Answer B is incorrect). Pemetrexed is an option, but the patient wants to start today or tomorrow, and he must begin vitamin B12 and folic acid supplementation a week before the first dose of pernetrexed (Answer C is incorrect). Oxaliplatin and gemcitabine is not a good choice because it has not shown benefit as second-line treatment, and the patient recently relapsed after receiving gemcitabine therapy (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: M.N.'s grandson comes with him to his next clinic visit; the grandson has concerns regarding his own risk of pancreatic adenocarcinoma and asks what he can do to minimize his risk. On further questioning, you learn that he is a 31-year-old man with no smoking history. He consumes two or three beers per week. He has hypertension that is currently well controlled with drugs and type I diabetes mellitus, which he developed at about age 27. He is 6'0" tall and weighs 111.4 kg (245 Ib) (body mass index 33.2 kg/m2). Which one of the following risk factors confers the greatest potential risk for the development of pancreatic adenocarcinoma for M.N.'s grandson?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The grandson has several risk factors for developing pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Type I diabetes mellitus is associated with a relative risk of 2.0 (Answer D is correct); this is greater than obesity with a body mass index greater than 30, which has a relative risk of 1.72 (Answer B is incorrect). Alcohol use is not directly associated with the development of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (Answer A is incorrect). The patient has no smoking history, so smoking is incorrect (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following options is best for monitoring M.N.'s grandson regarding development of pancreatic adenocarcinoma?
options: A. Undergo ultrasonography every 2 years starting at age 40.
B. Enroll in a screening and surveillance clinical trial.
C. Undergo a computed tomography scan with follow-up scans every 5 years.
D. Monitor CA 19-9 serum concentrations yearly.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is often advanced upon diagnosis and has a low survival rate, even for patients who undergo complete resection. A screening tool would be of significant use if it were sensitive and specific enough to detect early cancer. No screening recommendations exist for average-risk patients. The patient at average risk is someone with no risk factors for the development of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. For patients who are considered at high risk of an inherited syndrome or who have a family history, like the grandson, enrollment in a clinical trial that is evaluating screening and surveillance is recommended (Answer B is correct). Imaging of the pancreas is difficult,and sensitivity and specificity depend on the expertise of the person performing the test.Imaging with ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging are also not considered cost-effective (Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). Measurement of CA 19-9 is not specific enough because it may be elevated in benign biliary disease and several other types of cancer. In addition, 5% to 15% of the population cannot synthesize CA 19-9,resulting in a high false-negative rate (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 59-year-old woman calls the pharmacy, requesting information for symptom control for an outbreak of acne on her forehead and cheeks. The acne started about a week ago and seems to be getting worse. She describes it as looking "similar to the acne my son deals with" and adds that it itches. She received a prescription for erlotinib 100 mg/day 10 days ago, and the rash developed a couple of days after starting the drug. She vaguely remembers her oncologist talking about a rash and some drugs that she should start if the rash appeared. The following prescriptions were placed on file when erlotinib was filled: minocycline 100 mg, clindamycin lotion 1%, and hydrocortisone cream 1%.Which one of the following is the best recommendation for treatment of this patient's rash?
options: A. Keep the face moisturized and use benzoyl peroxide sparingly.
B. Take oral minocycline with the erlotinib.
C. Keep the face dry and apply hydrocortisone cream to the rash.
D. Use an emollient cream and topical clindamycin lotion.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The development of an acneiform rash with erlotinib treatment is common and can adversely affect QoL. The most important treatment recommendation is to keep the skin moist. Unlike acne, this is a dry rather than an oily rash. For patients with grade 1-2 epidermal growth factor (EGFR)-associated acneiform rash, topical antibiotics such as clindamycin 1% lotion ) should be used (Answer D is correct) before trying systemic antibiotics such as minocycline (Answer B is incorrect). Topical metronidazole and erythromycin have also been used; benzoyl peroxide should not be used because it has drying effects and is not helpful (Answer A is incorrect). Hydrocortisone cream is an option in grade 1-2 rash, but the face should be kept moist, not dry (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A 39-year-old woman recently received a diagnosis of insulinoma. Her laboratory values are within normal limits except for her glucose, which often drops to 40-50 mg/dL. Which one of the following therapeutic options is best for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Excess amounts of insulin are being excreted because of the patient's insulinoma,resulting in frequent hypoglycemia. Before surgical removal or drug treatment of any functioning insulinoma, the hormone overproduction must be addressed to avoid complications related to hypoglycemia (Answer A is incorrect).Diazoxide increases blood glucose and is the best-studied agent for use in insulinoma (Answer D is correct).Octreotide should be used with caution because it may suppress counter-regulatory hormones, resulting in worsening of the hypoglycemia (Answer B is incorrect).Although streptozocin can decrease insulin production, the effect is not immediate. in addition, chemotherapy is not first-line therapy, and every attempt should be made to resect the tumor first (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A 71-year-old woman received a diagnosis of localized pancreatic adenocarcinoma.She presents with jaundice and a serum bilirubin of 12 mg/dL, as well as nausea and abdominal pain. She is in fairly good health. Her surgeon thinks this tumor is resectable,although he may not be able to get clean margins around all areas of it. Which one of the following is the best plan for proceeding with treatment in this patient?
options: A. Biliary stent, chemoradiation, followed by surgery.
B. Chemotherapy, surgery, followed by chemoradiation.
C. Chemoradiation, biliary stent, followed by surgery.
D. Surgery, radiation, followed by chemotherapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Surgery offers the only possibility of cure for this patient, and the surgeon believes the umor is resectable. Because it is questionable whether adequate margins can be obtained, and because locoregional recurrence is very high in pancreatic adenocarcinoma, neoadjuvant chemoradiation therapy is advantageous in this situation.However, for a patient with jaundice and hyperbilirubinemia, preoperative biliary drainage and stenting are usually necessary if surgery is to be delayed, as in the patient undergoing chemotherapy or chemoradiation before surgery. Drainage and stenting do not improve postsurgical outcomes if surgery is needed immediately. This patient's surgery must be delayed for neoadjuvant chemoradiation (Answer A is correct). Further chemotherapy after surgery may be of benefit. Chemotherapy and surgery, followed by chemoradiation is not the best answer because surgery may be delayed by the chemotherapy, and the biliary obstruction should be addressed first (Answer B is incorrect). Chemoradiation after surgery is appropriate to decrease local recurrence,but chemotherapy alone is usually not administered before surgery in resectable disease. The biliary obstruction should be addressed first, and then chemoradiation administered before surgery (Answer C is incorrect). Surgery and radiation, followed by Chemotherapy is not the best answer because after biliary obstruction is addressed chemotherapy in conjunction with radiation has shown the best outcomes (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma has the best prognosis for long-term survival?
options: A. A 68-year-old woman with negative surgical margins, one lymph node metastasis, a 2.5-cm tumor, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group PS of 1.
B. A 72-year-old man with a 2-cm tumor, negative surgical margins, no positive lymph nodes, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group PS of 3.
C. A 56-year-old man with microscopic surgical margins, negative lymph nodes, a 1.3. cm tumor, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group PS of 1.
D. A 80-year-old woman with negative lymph nodes, microscopic surgical margins, a 2.3-cm tumor, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group PS of 2.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Prognostic features that give the best outcome for longterm survival include clear Purgical margins, tumor less than 2 cm, and negative lymph nodes. The 56-year-old man has the best prognosis for long-term survival because his tumor is less than 2 cm and he has negative lymph nodes (Answer C is correct). The 68-year-old woman does not have the best prognosis because her tumor is larger than 2 cm and she has one positive lymph hode, although her other tumor features are lower risk (Answer A is incorrect). The 72.yearold man has good tumor features, although his tumor is of borderline size. However,his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group PS is of concem, because he may have more problems postoperatively and with chemotherapy (Answer B is incorrect). The 80-yearold woman has a tumor greater than 2 cm with a borderline PS and microscopically positive surgical margins, so the prognosis is worse than that of the 56-year-oid man(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 52-year-old woman with a diagnosis of insulinoma is scheduled to undergo surgery in 3 days. She has hypertension that is treated with metoprolol. She is also taking aspirin and calcium with vitamin D. She was noted to be hypoglycemic during the workup and has been using a blood glucose monitor that documents her glucose concentration and the time it is tested. Her glucose concentrations range from 65 mg/dL to 138 mg/dL, with the lowest values around mid-morning. Which one of the following is the best management strategy for this patient?
options: B. Eat small meals throughout the day.
C. Administer tube feeds at night.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Hypoglycemia is the most common symptom of insulinomas and varies in severity among patients. This patient is scheduled to undergo surgery in 3 days' time. Eating small meals throughout the day is the best answer because of the short amount of time before she goes to surgery and the mild hypoglycemia she is experiencing (Answer B is correct). In the short term, her low blood glucose can be controlled by diet. Complete resection of the insulinoma should then normalize her blood glucose. Diazoxide and octreotide would be better choices if surgery were to be delayed and glucose needed to be controlled for a longer period (Answer A and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: A 56-year-old woman has a history of hypertension and gastroesophageal reflux disease. Her drugs are amlodipine 5 mg/day and ranitidine 150 mg two times/day. She was recently diagnosed with a carcinoid tumor with metastases noted in her lymph nodes and liver. Today, she complains of severe diarrhea and flushing. Which one of the following is the best option to control this patient's symptoms?
options: A. Loperamide 4 mg once and 2 mg by mouth every 2-4 hours.
B. Fluoxetine 20 mg by mouth daily.
C. Octreotide 100 mcg subcutaneously three times/ day.
D. Omeprazole 200 mg by mouth daily.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Flushing and diarrhea are symptoms of carcinoid syndrome and are caused by the release of serotonin, histamine, and tachykinins into the circulatory system. Octreotide is the best answer because it suppresses the release of these substances (Answer C is correct). Because serotonin is responsible for the diarrhea, loperamide does not treat the symptoms appropriately (Answer A is incorrect). Serotonin antagonists such as ondansetron are most likely to help treat diarrhea secondary to carcinoid syndrome, not selective serotonin receptor inhibitors like fluoxetine (Answer B is incorrect).Omeprazole is used to treat excessive acid production from gastrinomas and does not treat symptoms secondary to carcinoid tumors (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 62-year-old man has a history of complicated peptic ulcer disease, chronic diarrhea, and recent abdominal pain. An evaluation resulted in a new diagnosis of malignant gastrinoma. He will undergo surgical resection of his disease in 1 week.During this visit, the patient also states that he has heartburn, and he inquires about available options to help relieve this symptom. He has been sleeping in his armchair because of the discomfort. Which one of the following is the best treatment option for this patient?
options: A. Streptozocin intravenously 1 g/m2 before surgery.
B. Octreotide 100 mcg subcutaneously three times/ day.
C. Omeprazole 20 mg by mouth daily.
D. Lansoprazole 120 mg by mouth daily.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. High doses of proton pump inhibitors or histamine-2 receptor antagonists are the treatments of choice to control excess gastric acid secretion in patients with gastrinomas.High doses are required, so lansoprazole 120 mg is the best answer (Answer D is correct). Streptozocin intravenously 1 g/m2 before surgery is incorrect because the patient should receive surgery alone, not chemotherapy (Answer A is incorrect).Omeprazole 20 mg is a dose for peptic ulcer disease or gastroesophageal reflux disease and is not high enough to be effective for gastrinoma (Answer C is incorrect). Octreotide is usually used in combination with a proton pump inhibitor for patients who become refractory to proton pump inhibitors (Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: A 72-year-old man has received two cycles of gemcitabine and erlotinib for the treatment of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has developed an acneiform rash on his face and neck from this therapy. The patient was treating the rash with topical clindamycin 1% lotion and hydrocortisone 1% cream. Today, areas of this rash are very red, crusted, and inflamed, and the patient complains of intense itching in the affected area. The rash appears to be infected. The patient has no known drug allergies. Which one of the following is the best treatment approach for this patient?
options: A. Discontinue all chemotherapy and initiate tetracycline 500 mg two times/day.
B. Hold erlotinib and initiate minocycline 100 mg two times/day.
C. Continue all chemotherapy and initiate oral tetracycline 500 mg two times/day,
D. Reduce the erlotinib dose by 50% and initiate minocycline 100 mg two times/day,
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Development of rashes with EGFR inhibitor therapy is correlated with efficacy of therapy in many cancers, including colorectal, lung, and pancreatic. Therefore, the goal is to treat and control the rash as much as possible before reducing the dose or discontinuing therapy. However, if a grade 3 or 4 rash develops, the offending agent should be discontinued temporarily. Because the patient has a super infection of the rash,therapy needs to be held, and oral antibiotics should be initiated to treat the infection(Answer B is correct). There is no reason to discontinue gemcitabine; this leaves the patient with no cancer therapy and is not necessary because gemcitabine does not affect the rash (Answer A is incorrect). Continuing all chemotherapy and initiating oral tetracycline is not appropriate because the patient has a grade 3 rash (Answer C is jncorrect). Reducing the erlotinib dose and initiating minocycline is not the best answer because erlotinib should be held until the rash has resolved or at least resolved enough to be considered a grade 2 rash. At that time, erlotinib can be reinitiated, usually at 50% of the dose, and the rash can be monitored closely (Answer D is correct).

questions.question: A 56-year-old man recently received a diagnosis of metastatic pancreatic endocrine tumor (PET). He is in good health and takes only lisinopril 10 mg daily for hypertension and the occasional use of ranitidine and ibuprofen. Which one of the following therapies is best for this patient?
options: A. Streptozocin and doxorubicin therapy for 4 months or until progressive disease is documented.
B. Streptozocin, doxorubicin, and fluorouracil until best response is seen, then continue therapy for 4 months.
C. Streptozocin and fluorouracil until best response is seen; then switch to streptozocin and doxorubicin.
D. Streptozocin, doxorubicin, and fluorouracil combination therapy for 4 months or until progressive disease.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The standard of care for metastatic pancreatic endocrine tumors (PETs) is streptozocin,doxorubicin, and fluorouracil combination therapy until best response is seen; then continue therapy for 4 months. This therapy was assessed in three trials with response rates of 29% to 55% (Answer B is correct). Answer A and Answer D are incorrect,therapy should continue for 4 months after best response has been seen because response may take time to develop. Answer C is incorrect because streptozocin and doxorubicin were found to be better than streptozocin and fluorouracil, and sequential combination therapy has not been studied in clinical trials.

questions.question: As part of a multidisciplinary study group, you are involved in the creation of a protocol to test a new drug as first-line therapy in metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.Which one of the following study designs would generate the best data to evaluate the use of XA-2553 in the therapy of this disease?
options: A. XA-2553 compared with fluorouracil and leucovorin.
B. XA-2553 plus gemcitabine compared with BSC.
D. XA-2553 compared with gemcitabine monotherapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Standard therapy for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma is considered gemcitabine monotherapy. To prove that an investigational drug is as good as or better than gemcitabine, they should be compared in a head-to-head trial (Answer D is correct).XA-2553 compared with fluorouracil and leucovorin is not the best answer because it is not testing the drug against the standard of care (Answer A is incorrect). XA-2553 plus gemcitabine and XA-2553 compared with best supportive care) are not ethical because gemcitabine has proven benefits in first-line treatment (Answer B and Answer C are incorrect).

questions.question: A 54-year-old man is undergoing testing for a suspected PET. He is taking the following drugs: fluoxetine 20 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, metformin extended release 1000 mg daily, and loratadine 10 mg daily. During his diagnostic workup, which one of the following is best to instruct this patient to discontinue?
options: A. Omeprazole 7 days before testing gastrin concentrations.
B. Fluoxetine 10 days before testing serotonin concentrations.
C. Loratadine 24 hours before serotonin concentrations.
D. Metformin 48 hours before testing insulin concentrations.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. For workup of a PET, several tests are used to discern what type of PET it is. One of the lests for a gastrinoma is a serum gastrin concentration, so acid suppressive therapy must be discontinued 7 days before obtaining it to ensure accurate concentrations (Answer A is correct). Serotonin is seen in higher amounts in carcinoid tumors, but urinary concentrations are not affected by fluoxetine (Answer B is incorrect) or antihistamines(Answer C is incorrect). Diagnosis of an insulinoma is through a 72-hour fasting test, nof by measuring serum insulin concentrations (Answer D is incorrect). Serum insulin and glucose concentrations will not assist in diagnosis of the insulinoma but will help in the clinical care of the patient.

questions.question: A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma 3 months ago and is now receiving gemcitabine. Today, he presents with warmth and swelling in his right calf and subsequently receives a diagnosis of deep venous thrombosis. He is currently taking metformin extended release 1000 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, and omeprazole 20 mg daily. Which one of the following is the best treatment option for this patient at this time?
options: A. Discontinue gemcitabine therapy and begin warfarin.
B. Discontinue gemcitabine and begin enoxaparin.
C. Continue gemcitabine and begin enoxaparin.
D. Continue gemcitabine and begin unfractionated heparin
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Beginning a low-molecular-weight heparin is the best option in a patient with cancer who has a diagnosis of a venous thromboembolism (VTE). One trial showed that patients with cancer and VTE had better survival with a risk of death at 12 months of 20% for dalteparin versus 36% for oral coumarin derivatives. Gemcitabine should be Continued because developing a VTE is not a contraindication to therapy (Answer C is Correct; Answer B is incorrect). Continuing gemcitabine and beginning unfractionated heparin is not the best answer because unfractionated heparin has not been proved to lave greater benefits compared with low-molecular-weight heparins (Answer D is Incorrect).Discontinuing gemcitabine and initiating warfarin is incorrect because gemcitabine should be continued, and warfarin is not the best therapy for a VTE in a patient with cancer (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following patients with carcinoid of the colon is most likely to experience carcinoid syndrome?
options: A. Elevated urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) concentration, lymph node metastases, and a 2.4-cm tumor.
B. Elevated urinary 5-HIAA concentration, liver metastases, and a 2-cm tumor.
C. Elevated serum serotonin concentration, lymph node metastases, and a 2-cm tumor,
D. Elevated serum serotonin concentration, no metastases, and a 2.6-cm tumor.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The severity of carcinoid syndrome is correlated with the tumor size; elevated concentrations of urinary serotonin or its metabolite, 5-HIAA;} and whether the tumor has direct access to the systemic circulation. Most metabolic products are cleared by the liver; however, those produced by liver metastases may bypass first-pass metabolism and' pass directly into the hepatic vein. Therefore, elevated urinary S-HIAA concentration, liver metastases, and a 2-cm tumor is the most correct answer because liver metastases are present (Answer B is correct).Elevated urinary 5-HIAA concentration, lymph node metastases, and a 2.4-cm tumor; and elevated serum serotonin concentration, lymph nodes metastases, and a 2-cm tumor have metastases to the lymph nodes only, which are less likely to cause carcinoid syndrome (Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). Elevated serum serotonin concentrations, no metastases, and a 2.6- cm tumor has no metastases at all and is the least likely to cause carcinoid syndrome. In addition, urinary serotonin concentrations are measured, not serum concentrations (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 51-year-old woman was diagnosed with a PET 1 year ago and was originally reated with surgery. She now has a small locoregional recurrence (less than I cm) at the site of the original resection and a single metastatic lesion in the liver. She is in good health with a PS of 0. Which one of the following options is the best treatment of this patient's tumor recurrence?
options: A. Surgical resection of the primary tumor and liver metastasis.
B. Streptozocin and doxorubicin therapy until disease progression.
C. Streptozocin for 4 months followed by surgical resection of the tumor.
D. Octreotide monthly with resection of tumor and liver metastasis.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The NCCN recommendations are to resect the tumor and any metastases, if possible,because resection decreases symptoms, improves QoL, and prolongs survival (Answer A is correct). This recommendation includes recurrent disease. With a small tumor (less than I cm) and a single metastatic lesion, both areas are likely resectable. Therefore,streptozocin and doxorubicin therapy until disease progression with no surgical intervention is incorrect. (Answer B is incorrect) Octreotide monthly with resection of tumor and liver metastasis is incorrect; octreotide alone is used if the tumor is unresectable (Answer D is incorrect). Streptozocin monotherapy for 4 months or until disease progression is used in unresectable disease only (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A 56-year-old woman who lives in Chicago received a diagnosis of early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) about I month ago. She has a history of Rheumatoid arthritis, intravenous drug abuse for 10 years, and smoking one pack per week for 25 years. She consumes on average three beers daily with her dinner. Her diet consists of fast food about four times a week. A computerized tomography scan of the liver was negative for cirrhosis or ascites, and multiple areas of hepatic masses were appreciated.Which one of the following factors is most likely to be associated with HCC in this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Hepatitis B and C virus infections, cirrhosis, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity,diabetes, inherited liver disorders, and aflatoxin exposure are identified risk factors for HCC. This patient has a history of intravenous drug abuse, which puts her at increased risk of HBV and HCV infections. She also has a history of excessive alcohol consumption. With the lack of cirrhosis in this patient, HCV and alcohol consumption are less likely because most patients with HCC have cirrhosis before developing HCC(Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). About 30% to 50% of patients with HBV infection and patients exposed to aflatoxin have HCC without having cirrhosis.Aflatoxin is the least likely cause of her HCC because she lives in Chicago, which typically has cold weather (Answer B is incorrect). Based on her diet, she is less likely to have excessive consumption of aflatoxin. Therefore, HBV is the most likely cause of her HCC (Answer D is correct).

questions.question: A 62-year-old white man who lives in Little Rock, Arkansas, received a diagnosis of advanced stage HCC. He has a history of diabetes, high cholesterol, and intravenous drug abuse, and he drinks two or three beers every 2 weeks. His uncle was diagnosed with HCC at the age of 73. Which one of the following is most likely to be associated with HCC in this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Most HCC cases worldwide are associated with HBV or HBC. The associations with hepatic infections vary based on the region. This patient has a history of intravenous drug abuse; therefore, he has a higher risk of HBV or HCV infection. The United States has good surveillance and an HBV vaccination program, resulting in a lower incidence of HBV infection (Answer D is incorrect). Hepatitis C virus is usually associated with the incidence of HCC in the United States because of lack of vaccine availability to prevent HCV (Answer C is correct). This patient consumes only two or three beers every) weeks; therefore, excessive alcohol consumption is less likely to be the cause of HCC(Answer A is incorrect). He has an uncle with a history of HCC, but he is not a firstdegree relative. In addition, the uncle was given a diagnosis at age 73. Therefore, an inherited liver disorder is unlikely to be a significant risk factor for HCC (Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: A 48-year-old man lives in Africa where it is hot and humid most of the year. He has worked all of his life on a farm growing corn, and he consumes corn at least six times/week. About 2 months ago, he was diagnosed with advanced stage HCC. He consumes alcohol daily and denies any family history of cancer. A computerized tomography scan of the liver is negative for cirrhosis or ascites, and multiple areas of hepatic masses are appreciated. Which one of the following factors is most likely to cause HCC in this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Aflatoxin exposure is the most likely cause of this patient's HCC because he lives in a hot and moist region and eats corn (Answer B is correct). With the absence of cirrhosis in this patient, HCV, alcohol consumption, and inherited liver disorders are less likely because most patients with HCC from these causes have cirrhosis before developing HCC (Answer A, Answer C, and Answer D are incorrect). About 30% to 50% of patients with HBV infection and patients exposed to aflatoxin have HCC without having cirrhosis.

questions.question: Last week, a 42-year-old woman with a history of hypothyroidism and no other previous medical problems learned that she has HBV infection. She asks if she should be Screened for HCC at regular intervals now that she has HBV infection. Which one of the following recommendations is best for this patient regarding screening with a liver ultrasonography and a-fetoprotein (AFP) concentration for HCC?
options: A. Initiate screening now; then repeat every 24 months.
B. Initiate screening now; then repeat every 12 months.
C. Wait until she develops cirrhosis; then screen every 24 months.
D. Wait until she is 50 years old; then screen every 12 months.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Screening for HCC is recommended for high-risk patients. High-risk patients are those with cirrhosis or HBV infection. Patients eligible for screening are recommended to undergo screening every 6-12 months and not 24 months (Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). In addition, she does not need to wait to have cirrhosis because patients with HBV infection can progress to HCC without having cirrhosis (Answer C is incorecp).Screning is recommended in men older than 40 and for women older than 50. This patient has HBV, so she would be a candidate for screening at age 50, not now at age 42(Answer D is correct; Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: A 45-year-old man was recently diagnosed with HBV infection with elevated liver function tests. He has a medical history of diabetes and hyperlipidemia. He comes to you to receive counseling on the need for screening for HCC. Which one of the following recommendations is best for this patient regarding screening with liver ultrasonography and AFP concentration for HCC?
options: A. Initiate screening now; then every 24 months.
B. Initiate screening now; then every 12 months.
C. Wait until he develops cirrhosis; then screen every 24 months
D. Wait until he is 50 years old; then screen every 12 months.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. This patient is eligible for screening because of HBV infection and his age. He should undergo screening every 6-12 months (Answer B is correct), not every 24 months(Answer A is incorrect). He is a candidate for screening regardless of history of cirrhosis because some HBV infections can progress to HCC without causing cirrhosis (Answer C is incorrect). Men at high risk should begin screening at age 40, so waiting until he is 50 years old is incorrect (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 68-year-old man receives a diagnosis of advanced HCC. He has a medical history of cirrhosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoporosis. Magnetic resonance imaging of his liver is positive for tumor in the liver, mild extrahepatic involvement, and moderate ascites. His liver function tests are aspartate aminotransferase 60 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 76 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 160 U/L, total bilirubin 2.2 mg/dL, and albumin 3.1 g/dL. He has an international normalized ratio of 1.8. Further workup reveals grade 1 hepatic encephalopathy. Which one of the following is the best treatment option for this patient's HCC?
options: B. Sorafenib 400 mg by mouth daily.
C. Sorafenib 400 mg by mouth two times/day.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. This patient is not a candidate for chemoembolization for treatment of his HCC because Of non-preserved liver function tests and HCC with extrahepatic spread (Answer D is Incorrect). He is not eligible for sorafenib because of Child-Pugh C classification. The Child-Pugh score is based on several factors including bilirubin, INR, albumin, and plesence of ascites and hepatic encephalopathy. The patient has moderate ascites, grade I hepatic encephalopathy, elevated total bilirubin and INR, and low albumin; therefore his score is 11, and he has Child-Pugh C cirrhosis Therefore, sorafenib 400 mg by mouth Iwo times/day is incorrect (Answer C is incorrect). Because of his elevated total bilirubin concentration, the dose could be adjusted to 400 mg once daily if he were eligible for treatment (Answer B is incorrect). Survival of patients with advanced liver complications is low. In addition, well-proved treatment options in these patients are Jacking. Therefore, he should be considered for a clinical trial, from which he may benefit (Answer A is correct).

questions.question: Which one of the following groups of parameters is best for monitoring the safety of sorafenib?
options: A. Stool frequency, cholesterol values, blood pressure, thyroid function tests.
B. Blood pressure, thyroid function tests, extremities examination, hemoglobin AIC.
C. Stool frequency, blood pressure, thyroid function tests, extremities examination.
D. Stool frequency, cholesterol values, extremities examination, hemoglobin AIC.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Diarrhea, fatigue, and hand-foot syndrome are some of the significant adverse effects of sorafenib and are common reasons for a sorafenib dose reduction. Therefore, it is important to monitor stool frequency for diarrhea. Examination of extremities helps identify hand-foot syndrome. Any agent that inhibits vascular endothelial growth factor has high blood pressure as an adverse effect. Therefore, it is important that a patient's blood pressure be monitored at home and during clinic visits. Hypothyroidism has been reported in patients taking sorafenib. Therefore, thyroid function tests should be monitored at regular intervals. They also may help rule out one of the causes of fatigue commonly seen in patients taking sorafenib. Therefore, Answer C is correct. Blood glucose changes, and therefore hemoglobin AIC changes, are not typically seen with Sorafenib (Answer B and Answer D are incorrect). High cholesterol is not seen with sorafenib therapy (Answer A and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: A 40-year-old woman with a history of seizures, diabetes, and asthma is enrolled in a clinical trial of adjuvant sorafenib treatment for early-stage HCC. She had lost 10 kg since liver resection and was mildly underweight at 62 kg before starting sorafenib. At sorafenib initiation, her pertinent laboratory values were as follows: white blood cell count 7.8 x 103 cells/ mm3, hemoglobin 13 g/dL, platelet count 198,000 cells/ mm3,sodium 132 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 22 mg/ dL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL, glucose 152 mg/dL, albumin 3.2 g/dL, aspartate aminotransferase 60 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 72 U/L, and total bilirubin 1.9 mg/dL. Her drugs were phenytoin, glipizide, fluticasone inhaler, and albuterol inhaler as needed. The patient was initiated on sorafenib 400 mg orally two times/day about 19 days ago. Today she has severe sorafenib-induced handfoot syndrome, diarrhea, low phosphate concentration, and neutropenia. Which one of the following is the most likely explanation for the severe sorafenib toxicity seen in this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The sorafenib dose should be reduced in patients with elevated total bilirubin, low albumin, or reduced creatinine clearance. This patient has a moderately elevated total bilirubin of 1.9 mg mg/dL (Answer B is correct). The patient's sorafenib-induced severe toxicity is likely caused by reduced clearance of the drug. She has a low albumin concentration of 3.2 g/dL, but the dose needs no adjustment until albumin is less than 2.5 g/dL (Answer C is incorrect). The patient has abnormal renal function; however, her calculated creatinine clearance is 46 mL/minute, which is higher than a creatinine clearance of 40 mL/minute or less needed to consider sorafenib dose adjustment(Answer A is incorrect). Sorafenib interacts with strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors.Phenytoin is a CYP3A4 inducer, but phenytoin is likely to reduce sorafenib concentrations, not increase toxicity (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 59-year-old man receives a diagnosis of HCC after biopsy of the liver. At presentation, he had no abdominal symptoms and an AFP of 150 ng/mL. Magnetic resonance imaging of his liver shows tumor in two lobes of the liver of 1.5 cm and 2.5 cm. The patient has an aspartate aminotransferase of 29 U/L, alanine aminotransferase of 35 U/L, international normalized ratio of 1.1, and total bilirubin of 1.1 mg/dL. Which one of the following describes the best treatment options for this patient?
options: A. Hepatic resection or liver transplantation.
B. Liver transplantation or radiofrequency ablation (RFA).
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Based on his presentation, this patient has early-stage HCC. Therefore, he is not a candidate for hepatic resection (Answer A is incorrect). Hepatic resection is considered for patients with very early-stage HCC. He is a candidate for liver transplantation because he has less than three lesions of less than 3 cm each. He also can be considered for RFA if liver transplantation is not possible (Answer B is correct).Chemoembolization is reserved for intermediate or advanced-stage patients (Answer C and Answer D are incorrect). Sorafenib is indicated for patients with advanced-stage disease, so this answer is also incorrect (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 91 and 92 pertain to the following case. O.K., a 59-year-old woman, receives a diagnosis of HCC based on imaging and AFP concentration. At presentation, she had abdominal pain; a physical examination was negative for ascites or other symptoms. Overall, O.K. is in good general physical condition and able to complete her daily activities without difficulty. A magnetic resonance imaging of the liver is positive for tumor in the liver and mild extrahepatic involvement. Her liver function tests are international normalized ratio 1.2, prothrombin time 14.6 seconds (within normal limits for the institution), albumin 3.8 g/dL, aspartate aminotransferase 45 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 40 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 110 U/L, and total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL. Her chemistry panel is normal except for chloride 108 mEq/L, serum creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, and blood glucose 140 mg/dL. Which one of the following is the best description of O.K.'s hepatic status and performance status, respectively?
options: A. Child-Pugh A and performance status 3.
B. Child-Pugh B and performance status 1.
C. Child-Pugh B and performance status 3.
D. Child-Pugh A and performance status 1.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. It is important to classify the patient's hepatic and PS to determine optimal HCC treatment. The patient has no ascites or hepatic encephalopathy, and her liver function tests are normal; therefore, her score is 5, and she has Child-Pugh A cirrhosis (Answer B) and Answer C are incorrect). The patient is fairly active and does not have limited daily pctivity. She is in good general physical condition; therefore, her PS is 1 or better(Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). A PS of 3 is defined as being inactive most of the day. Answer D is correct because the patient has Child-Pugh A cirrhosis and a PS ofl

questions.question: Which one of the following is the best treatment option for O.K.'s HCC?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. This patient has advanced-stage HCC because of mild symptoms, good general physical condition, Child-Pugh A cirrhosis, and extrahepatic spread. Therefore, she is a candidate for systemic therapy with sorafenib (Answer D is correct). Based on her advanced HCC stage, she is not a candidate for liver transplantation (Answer A is incorrect).Radiofrequency ablation is an option primarily for early stage HCC (Answer B is incorrect). Because she has extrahepatic spread, she is not a candidate for chemoembolization (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 93-95 pertain to the following case. S.G. is a 62-year-old white woman with a history of resected stage III colorectal cancer(CRC) diagnosed in January 2009. She did not receive adjuvant chemotherapy. In May 2010,she had surveillance computed tomography scans that showed two solitary 4-cm lesions in the right hepatic lobe. Computed tomography-guided fine-needle aspiration of both lesions was consistent with adenocarcinoma from colon cancer. Which one of the following is the most significant poor prognostic factor for S.G.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The patient has three negative prognostic variables for surgical resection of the hepatic metastases: age 60 or older, disease-free interval of less than 2 years, and stage III colon cancer, which indicates that the primary tumor has extended into the serosa and involves the lymph nodes. The most significant of these variables is the stage of her primary tumor, with a relative risk score of 1.5 (Answer A is correct). The second most significant prognostic variable for this patient is disease-free interval, with a relative risk of 1.4 (Answer C is incorrect). The presence of more than four hepatic metastases has a relative risk of 1.6; however, this patient does not have more than four hepatic metastases (Answer D is incorrect). Furthermore, her hepatic metastases are less than 5 cm (relative risk 1.3); therefore, Answer B is incorrect.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the best description of S.G.'s prognostic risk category and corresponding prognostic variables in addition to the stage of her primary tumor?
options: B. High; age, size of liver metastases.
C. Intermediate; sex, size, and number of metastases present.
D. High; number and size of liver metastases, disease free interval.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. In addition to the stage of the primary tumor, this patient has two negative prognostic variables for surgical resection of the hepatic metastases: age 60 or older and diseasefree interval of less than 2 years. Therefore, her risk category is intermediate (three or four variables), and Answer A is correct. The patient does not fall in the high-risk ategory because she does not have five to seven prognostic variables (Answer B and Answer D are incorrect). Sex is not a negative prognostic factor, and she does not have four or more metastatic lesions (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following therapies provides the optimal survival advantage for S.G. as supported by the current literature?
options: D. Neoadjuvant hepatic artery infusion (HAI) therapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Complete surgical resection is the best answer (Answer C is correct). Many studies have evaluated the definitive role of resection for hepatic metastases caused by colorectal fancer (CRC) and have shown conclusive benefit in these patients. Resection is the only Chance for cure in this patient. The evidence to support selective internal radiation lreatment for this patient is lacking (Answer A is incorrect). Current data support Consideration of this intervention in patients with unresectable disease in combination With HAI therapy. The evidence to support neoadjuvant systemic chemotherapy of heoadjuvant HAI therapy is strongest in patients with initially unresectable disease(Answer B and Answer D are incorrect). These interventions can be considered for Patients who are resection candidates; however, the evidence is stronger for a perioperative systemic chemotherapy approach without HAI. Neoadjuvant therapy for this patient can be considered if she decides against initial resection.

questions.question: A 69-year-old man has a history of resected stage III CRC diagnosed in January 2012. The patient had two solitary I.5-cm lesions in the right hepatic lobe; these were also resected. Six months later, the patient is seen for follow-up and has recurrent CRC hepatic metastases. Which one of the following is the best therapy for the patient at this time?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Radiofrequency ablation is the best answer (Answer B is correct). Radiofrequency ablation has been studied in patients with hepatic recurrence after initial resection for hepatic metastases secondary to CRC. It has also been studied in combination with resection and has shown better results than RFA alone. Cryotherapy has been used in combination with liver resection when not all disease can be resected; however, its use has been abandoned because it has a higher complication rate than RFA and inherent limitations (Answer A is incorrect). Transarterial chemoembolization has been primarily studied for the medical management of patients with initially unresectable CRC hepatio metastases, not in patients with recurrent hepatic metastases. Furthermore, most of the evidence for TACE is in the management of HCC, not CRC hepatic metastases (Answer C is incorrect).
