Selective internal radiation therapy has been studied in combination with HAI therapy for unresectable hepatic metastases, but not in initially resectable disease(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 97 and 98 pertain to the following case, J.B. is a 48-year-old white man who presents with stage IV CRC with an intact primary right colon tumor and four hepatic metastases that involve four hepatic segments identified by imaging. At presentation he has a normal complete blood cell count and chemistry panel except for creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 212 U/L, and carcinoembryonic antigen 65 ng/mL (baseline 2 ng/mL). His performance status is 2.97. Which one of the following is the most significant factor suggesting a poor prognosis for surgery for J.B?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. A prospective study of 544 patients revealed that poor performance status, followed by elevated alkaline phosphatase concentration, more than four involved liver segments,presence of extrahepatic metastases, right-sided primary liver metastases location,elevated prothrombin time, and resection of primary lesion had significant prognostic value in patients with unresected liver metastases from CRC. Therefore, performance status is correct (Answer A is correct). The number of hepatic segments involved is an important prognostic factor, especially because this patient's lesions involve multiple lobes of the liver; however, this is not the most significant factor (Answer B is incorrect). The presence of an intact primary tumor and the location of the primary tumor are important prognostic factors; nevertheless, they are not as statistically significant as poor performance status (Answer C and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the best first-line strategy for management of J.B.'s CRC hepatic metastases?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Palliative systemic chemotherapy is the best-studied approach for this patient (Answer D is correct). The patient is not the best candidate for a surgical resection for his hepatic metastases or for his primary tumor because he has many poor prognostic factors (poor performance status, elevated alkaline phosphatase concentration, no prior chemotherapy for liver metastases, primary tumor intact, and right-sided colon location) (Answer A is incorrect). The evidence to support neoadjuvant HAI therapy alone is poor, and it is marginally effective (Answer B is incorrect). Radiofrequency ablation has been studied in patients with CRC and hepatic metastases; however, because of the lack of definitive efficacy data to support the use of this approach, it is not the best initial medical management for this patient (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: You are an investigational drug pharmacist in oncology working to develop a protocol to evaluate the effectiveness of perioperative chemotherapy including a new platinum-containing agent in hepatic metastases compared with oxaliplatin. This will be a large multicenter study. Which one of the following best describes criteria for patient inclusion in this study?
options: A. Four or fewer liver metastases, PS of 2 or less, no extrahepatic tumor.
B. Initially unresectable disease, no major hepatic or renal insufficiency, PS of I or less.
C. More than four liver metastases, initially resectable disease, no prior oxaliplatin chemotherapy.
D. Initially resectable disease, four or fewer liver metastases, presence of extrahepatic tumor.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The best criteria are four or fewer liver metastases, performance status of 2 or less, and no extrahepatic tumor (Answer A is correct). When referring to currently published literature, important study inclusion criteria that should be integrated into the proposed study are four or fewer liver metastases, performance status of 2 or less, no detectable extrahepatic tumor, no previous oxaliplatin chemotherapy, and no major hepatic or renal jnsufficiency. Therefore, Answer B, Answer C, and Answer D are incorrect because they do not contain all three criteria.

questions.question: A 50-year-old African American man presents in March 2007 with bowel perforation and receives a diagnosis of stage IIB rectal cancer. He has a primary resection followed by 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy because of the high-risk pathologic features of the resected specimen. In February 2010, routine surveillance imaging shows one 10-cm liver lesion in the right lobe and two distinct 3-cm liver lesions in the left lobe confirmed by biopsy as adenocarcinoma of the colon. All laboratory results are within normal limits except alkaline phosphatase 300 U/L. The patient is a candidate for resection. Which one of the following is the best systemic chemotherapy option along with resection for this patient?
options: A. Neoadjuvant irinotecan, fluorouracil, and leucovorin.
C. Perioperative oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Perioperative oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin is the best answer (Answer C is correct). Perioperative chemotherapy was evaluated in a randomized study that revealed p significantly better progression-free survival for perioperative chemotherapy than with tesection alone. Studies evaluating neoadjuvant irinotecan, fluorouracil, and leucovorin;and adjuvant fluorouracil and leucovorin have not shown a significant progression-free survival advantage over resection alone (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect)Perioperative fluorouracil and leucovorin is not the best answer because it is known that fuorouracil and leucovorin alone are not sufficient; the addition of oxaliplatin to this backbone is necessary to provide improved response rates and an overall survival advantage (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 66-year-old man presents with unresectable HCC. His largest liver tumor is 6.5 cm. Scans for portal thrombosis and extrahepatic spread are negative. He has a total bilirubin of 1.6 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase 38 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 45 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 152 U/L, and creatinine clearance of 32 mL/minute. The patient has Child- Pugh B cirrhosis and a PS of 1. Which one of the following is the best treatment option for this patient?
options: B. TACE consisting of standard chemotherapy.
C. TACE consisting of doxorubicin-eluting beads.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. This patient is a candidate for TACE because his tumor is larger than 5 cm. In addition,he does not have portal thrombosis, extrahepatic tumor, and Child-Pugh C cirrhosis.Standard TACE has been compared with TACE containing doxorubicin-eluting beads in a phase Il trial. This trial showed that TACE with doxorubicineluting beads was better tolerated than TACE consisting of standard chemotherapy and provided a similar response rate (Answer C is correct; Answer B is incorrect). In addition, doxorubicineluting beads had a potential advantage (better response rate) in patients with ChildPugh B liver disease and good performance status. Transarterial embolization could be considered for this patient, but TACE provides better survival for unresectable HCC than transarterial embolization (Answer A is incorrect). Sorafenib should be considered in patients who are not candidates for TACE (Answer D is incorrect). In addition, he has moderately elevated total bilirubin and declining renal function, which puts him at increased risk of toxicity, and his sorafenib dosage would need to be reduced.

questions.question: Questions 102-106 pertain to the following case. J.J. is a 57-year-old man who is being followed by his primary care physician for a nodular-appearing lesion on his right tonsil and leukoplakia of his left lateral tongue.The patient has a history of Helicobacter pylori ulcers, herpes simplex type 1, and mononucleosis at age 15. He has an 84 packs /year smoking history, is still smoking, and denies any desire or effort to quit. Additional relevant social history includes being divorced with two grown children and an unknown number of sexual partners. He reports occasional pain from the tongue lesion. Human papillomavirus (HPV)-16 is detected in the tongue lesion. J.J. states that for about the past 5 months he has been having constant left ear and neck pain with a palpable left neck mass. He is complaining of odynophagia for the last few weeks and pain on his tongue. He also spits blood on a daily basis. J.J. denies any changes in his voice, difficulty breathing, recent weight loss,and night sweats. In addition to the subjective information reported by J.J., which one of the following objective findings is the most consistent with a diagnosis of head and neck cancer?
options: A. Presence of H. pylori in gastrointestinal ulcer.
B. Infection with HPV-16 in the tongue lesion.
C. Herpes simplex infection of the oral cavity.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The correct answer is infection with HPV-16 in the tonsil lesion, which is a well-known risk factor for head and neck cancer (Answer B is correct). Presence of H. pylori in gastrointestinal ulcer is incorrect because H. pylori is not associated with an increased lisk of head and neck cancer (Answer A is incorrect). Herpes simplex infection of the Oral cavity is associated with other types of cancer, but not head and neck cancer(Answer C is incorrect). Palpable neck mass is incorrect because it is nonspecific and Inay indicate other problems (e.g., lymphoma, infection) (Answer D is incorrect),

questions.question: J.J. eventually receives a diagnosis of stage IVa moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil. The mass is not amenable to resection. Which one of the following treatment options is most appropriate for J.J.?
options: B. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by radiation therapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. In unresectable stage IVa head and neck cancer, concurrent chemoradiation is the lreatment of choice (Answer C is correct). Combined modality therapy improves Outcomes significantly compared with radiation therapy alone (Answer D is incorrect)Chemotherapy alone is less effective than chemoradiation therapy, but it can be Considered in a patient who is not a good candidate for radiation therapy or who refuses radiation (Answer A is incorrect). Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by radiation is also inferior to concurrent chemoradiation therapy (Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: J.J. presents to the chemotherapy infusion suite for his first cycle of cisplatin 100 mg/m2 intravenously every 3 weeks. His chief complaint is pain in the tongue, neck, ear,and headaches. He also reports dysphagia. Which one of the following assessments is best to perform for J.J.?
options: A. Complete metabolic panel to assess nutrition status.
B. Liver enzyme panel to evaluate dose of cisplatin.
C. Dental examination to evaluate for dental caries.
D. Skin examination to evaluate for maculopapular rash.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Nutritional deficiencies are common in patients with head and neck cancer and are exacerbated by oral symptoms such as pain and dysphagia, so a complete metabolio panel to assess nutrition status is correct (Answer A is correct). Cisplatin causes nephrotoxicity, not hepatotoxicity, so a liver enzyme panel to evaluate cisplatin dose is incorrect (Answer B is incorrect). A dental examination to evaluate for dental caries is not a critical evaluation before chemotherapy for a symptomatic patient (Answer C is incorrect). A skin examination to evaluate for maculopapular rash is incorrect because a maculopapular rash is associated with cetuximab therapy, not cisplatin (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: J.J. reports to the chemotherapy infusion suite for cycle two of cisplatin. He denies any nausea and vomiting with the first cycle, but he is found to be hypotensive with a blood pressure of 75/56 mm Hg. His serum creatinine concentration is also elevated at 1.7 g/dL, and his calculated creatinine clearance is 55 mL/minute. Which one of the following is the best recommendation to the team?
options: A. Proceed with chemotherapy as planned.
D. Hold chemotherapy and institute intravenous hydration.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Hold chemotherapy and institute intravenous hydration to correct the hypotension and serum creatinine is the best option (Answer D is correct). Proceed with chemotherapy as planned is incorrect because cisplatin requires dose reduction for creatinine clearance less than 60 mL/minute (Answer A is incorrect). Although either reducing the cisplatin dose by 25% or changing cisplatin to carboplatin may be correct once the patient's performance status improves, the best approach for now is to hold chemotherapy and institute intravenous hydration (Answer B and Answer C are incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following patient-related characteristics of J.J. presents the most significant barrier to achieving the best response to treatment and could be included as part of ongoing public health campaigns that support disease prevention?
options: B. Unknown number of sexual partners.
C. Symptoms present for 5 months before diagnosis.
D. Latent herpes simplex I infection.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Smoking cessation and safe sex practices are important ongoing initiatives of public health experts. Providing education about the signs/symptoms of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN) could also be an important intervention in patients at high risk of developing SCCHN. However, continued smoking during treatment adversely affects treatment response (Answer A is correct). Although a high number of sexual partners, which cannot be ruled out in this patient because the actual number is unknown, and latent herpes simplex 1 infection are both risk factors for HPV-16 infection, they are incorrect because they do not change his response to treatment(Answer B and Answer D are incorrect). The patient's HPV-16 positivity is already known and is a good prognostic factor for SCCHN. Having symptoms for a prolonged period without a diagnosis puts the patient at risk of having more advanced disease at diagnosis but does not necessarily translate to a poorer response to treatment (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 107 and 108 pertain to the following case. P.L. is a 54-year-old man who has stage IVa squamous cell carcinoma of the base of the tongue. The patient has just completed standard chemoradiation therapy with every-3-week high-dose cisplatin and is complaining of significant pain in the oral cavity. He appears dehydrated; his oral cavity is very dry and has patches of leukoplakia and crusting on the right side of the base of his tongue with a yellowish exudate. Which one of the following treatments is best for P.L.'s symptoms?
options: A. Over-the-counter menthol/alcohol mouthwash, swish and spit two times/day.
B. Saliva substitute, swish and spit as needed.
C. Nystatin mouthwash, swish and spit three times/ day for 10 days.
D. Salt-and-soda rinse, swish and spit as needed.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The presence of leukoplakia, yellowish exudate, crusting, and significant pain suggest the patient has more than simple xerostomia and likely has oral candidiasis. Of the treatment options listed, nystatin mouthwash is most appropriate; although some centers treat with fluconazole (Answer C is correct). Over-the-counter menthol/alcohol mouthwash is not recommended because it can cause worsening of xerostomia (Answel A is incorrect). Saliva substitute treats only the xerostomia symptom, not the clinical problem (Answer B is incorrect). Salt-and-soda rinses, although a useful preventive measure for mucositis, does not treat oral candidiasis (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: P.L.'s oral symptoms are a barrier to adherence to his chronic oral drugs. Which one of the following interventions would have the greatest impact on ensuring P.L.'s adherence to his drugs?
options: A. Evaluate the necessity of all chronic oral drugs in his regimen.
B. Change as many oral drugs to liquid formulations as possible.
C. Counsel him on the importance of adherence to his drugs.
D. Ensure he has an adequate supply of his drugs at home.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Although all the choices provided are important to put the patient in the best position for adherence to his regimen, the best intervention is the one that makes it easy for him to ingest his medications, changing drugs to liquid formulations when possible (Answer B is correct). Evaluating all chronic drugs in his regimen is an important first step in the process; however, an evaluation without subsequent streamlining of medication and changing to liquid formulations will not have the most significant impact on adherence(Answer A is incorrect). Counseling the patient is important to reinforce the necessity of adherence; however, education alone will not facilitate drug ingestion (Answer C is incorrect). Similarly, ensuring that the patient has an adequate supply of drugs is certainly important, but the supply will go untaken if not in a formulation that is palatable to the patient (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 109-112 pertain to the following case. T.R. is a 56-year-old man with newly diagnosed stage Il squamous cell carcinoma of the supraglottic/transglottic larynx. His wife states that it was difficult to get T.R. to keep his scheduled appointment because of the 3-hour drive to the clinic and her husband's fear of chemotherapy ever since his sister died 5 years ago of breast cancer. T.R. will not admit that he is fearful of toxicities, but he does report that he is unwilling to compromise his role as the lead singer in his neighborhood band. T.R. has a history of atrial fibrillation and currently takes warfarin 5 mg daily; he also has type 2 diabetes mellitus and takes metformin 500 mg two times/day and glipizide 5 mg daily. He has fainted twice in the past month because of hypoglycemic episodes. T.R. is presented with both surgical and chemoradiotherapy options for the treatment of his disease. Which one of the following is the most likely reason why T.R. prefers a surgical approach?
options: A. Improved survival compared with chemoradiation.
B. Significant long-term toxicities with chemoradiation.
D. More frequent follow-up visits with chemoradiation.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Significant long-term toxicities with chemoradiation are the most likely reason (Answer B is correct). Adverse effects (AEs) are more common with chemoradiation, including secondary cancers, increased myelotoxicity, skin AEs, xerostomia, and mucositis. In early-stage disease, surgery and chemoradiation are equivalent in survival outcomes.Therefore, improved survival compared with chemoradiation is not the best choice(Answer A is incorrect). Surgical resection does not necessarily guarantee avoidance of chemotherapy because chemotherapy is employed if disease recurs (Answer C is incorrect). Chemoradiation, although initially requiring daily visits for 6-7 weeks to receive radiation treatment, mandates the same period of follow-up with the physician afer therapy completion. However, there is no guarantee that surgery will be uncomplicated and will not require frequent visits for instruction on the use of the electrolarynx, nutrition support, and percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy tube.Therefore, more frequent follow-up visits with chemoradiation is incorrect (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: T.R.'s chemoradiation regimen includes high-dose cisplatin and continuous infusion fluorouracil. Which one of the following interventions is most important while monitoring T.R. during chemoradiation?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. All the answer choices present plausible outcomes of interactions between the prescribed chemotherapy regimen and the patient's chronic oral drugs. Reduction of cisplatin dose suggests that there is added nephrotoxicity with cisplatin and metformin (Answer A is incorrect). Prescription of sunscreen suggests that sunscreen should be used for patients who are susceptible to the enhanced photosensitivity caused by sulfonylureas and fluorouracil (Answer B is incorrect). Addition of anti-dyspepsia drugs acknowledges that both metformin and cisplatin can cause dyspepsia (Answer D is incorrect).Reduction of warfarin dose, however, is the most well-documented and serious drug Imteraction listed, that of the potential for elevated INR from adding fluorouracil to warfarin therapy, and is the correct choice (Answer C is correct).

questions.question: While on the Internet, T.R.'s wife found information suggesting that amifostine should be used to prevent mucositis in patients treated with chemoradiation. Which one of the following is the most important education you can provide to explain why amifostine is not appropriate for her husband?
options: A. Amifostine has not been shown to consistently prevent mucositis in patients treated with chemoradiation.
B. Amifostine causes hypotension during administration and is unsafe given his history of hypoglycemia.
C. Amifostine may interfere with the efficacy of his chemotherapy treatment.
D. Mucositis can be treated with other agents that are supported by more rigorous scientific evidence.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. As a preventive agent for chemoradiation-induced mucositis, inconsistent evidence has been reported for amifostine, and for evidence-based decision-making, this is the most important supporting rationale for not using amifostine for this patient (Answer A is correct). The patient's history of hypoglycemia may be of concern depending on his condition at the time that amifostine is administered because of the hypotensive effects of amifostine, but this is not a strong reason to avoid amifostine use (Answer B is incorrect). Amifostine reduces the therapeutic efficacy of chemoradiatio is incorrect because this is a theoretical concern that has not been proved (Answer C is incorrect).Mucositis can be treated with other agents, such as the compounded mouthwashes;however, these various formulae have not been rigorously evaluated in controlled clinical trials; therefore, this answer is incorrect (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: T.R. selects total laryngectomy with radical neck dissection for treatment of his cancer. The pathology report indicates moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx; the tumor measures 3 cm x 2.5 cm x 1.2 cm with involvement of the false cord, true cord, and the anterior commissure. Lymphovascular invasion is not present; however, perineural invasion is observed, and two of 46 resected lymph nodes are positive. Which one of the following is the best next step in T.R.'s treatment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. One advantage of primary surgical management of head and neck cancer is the potential to better evaluate the extent of the patient's disease. This patient, who has extensive extracapsular spread of his disease, would benefit from further therapy. Concurrent chemoradiation therapy improves outcomes compared with radiation therapy alone, for both adjuvant treatment and as primary treatment in loco-regionally advanced disease(Answer C is correct). Because loco-regional recurrence is the primary concern for this patient, local treatment with radiation therapy is necessary, and chemotherapy alone is insufficient (Answer D is incorrect). No further treatment is necessary is incorrect because the patient does require additional treatment (Answer A is incorrect). Finally,chemoradiation is superior to radiation therapy, so radiation therapy alone is incorrect(Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 113 and 114 pertain to the following case. M.K. is a 58-year-old man with stage IVa oropharyngeal cancer who is offered treatment with chemoradiation. His tumor biopsy reveals that his cancer is positive for wild type KRAS. He works full-time as a self-employed general contractor and does not have health insurance. His only comorbidity is mild hypertension, which is treated with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Which one of the following is the best drug and supporting rationale to give M.K. concurrently with radiation?
options: A. Cetuximab because it is not myelosuppressive.
B. Cetuximab because it causes less nausea/vomiting than cisplatin.
C. Cisplatin because it is administered on a more convenient schedule than cetuximab.
D. Cisplatin because it is less costly than cetuximab.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The correct answer is cisplatin because it is less costly than cetuximab (Answer D is correct). This patient is unlikely to be able to afford the significant cost of cetuximab therapy. Cetuximab is administered on a weekly basis, whereas cisplatin is recommended on an every-3-week schedule; this is an advantage for this patient, who depends on keeping a steady work schedule to maintain his income. However, the significant cost difference between cisplatin and cetuximab has much greater influence on drug selection; particularly for a patient who must pay the full cash price of the therapy (Answer C is incorrect). Although cetuximab is not myelosuppressive and causes less nausea and vomiting than cisplatin, these AEs can be prevented and managed. (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect)

questions.question: On further discussion, M.K, reveals that he is comfortable using his significant savings to pay for the cost of cetuximab therapy. He also knows that he will need to come to the hospital daily for radiation therapy treatments. With this new information,which one of the following is the strongest reason why cetuximab- based therapy should be selected for M.K.?
options: A. Cetuximab-based therapy is more effective than cisplatin-based therapy.
B. His tumor overexpresses wild-type KRAS.
C. Cetuximab is less likely to increase radiation-associated toxicity than cisplatin.
D. The dose of cetuximab does not need to be adjusted for renal insufficiency.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Cetuximab is less likely to increase radiation-associated toxicity than cisplatin (Answer C is correct). Cisplatin has been extensively studied as part of chemoradiation, with many trials repeatedly showing its benefit for patients with locally advanced head and neck cancer. It is not known whether cisplatin-based chemoradiation is as effective as, or more effective than, cetuximab-based radiotherapy because the two have never been compared (Answer A is incorrect). The patient's tumor must have wild-type KRAS to respond to cetuximab; however, no trial has evaluated whether this influences response to cisplatin (Answer B is incorrect). This young patient's only comorbidity is mild hypertension. He is unlikely to have renal insufficiency, so the fact that cetuximab does not need adjustment for renal insufficiency does not matter (Answer D is incorrect). In addition, in the presence of renal insufficiency, the cisplatin dose could be adjusted.

questions.question: Questions 115-117 pertain to the following case. W.E. is a 72-year-old man who is diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in the left submandibular neck. Computed tomography identified a 2.5 cm x 2 cm mass abutting the left submandibular gland, mildly prominent lymph nodes in the neck, and a small 4-mm pulmonary nodule in the right middle lobe. When his case was presented at the multidisciplinary tumor board meeting, the consensus was that the primary source of the cancer was undetermined and recommendation was made to check the HPV status of the neck tumor. From a pharmacist's perspective, which one of the following is the most important area of research needed to translate W.E.'s HPV status into improved patient outcomes?
options: A. To decide if a particular drug should be used to treat a squamous cell cancer of the head and neck that is HPV-16 positive.
B. To evaluate HPV-16 viral load on prognosis.
C. To evaluate the effect of HPV vaccine on prognosis.
D. To administer HPV vaccine if negative.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Human papillomavirus-16-positive head and neck cancers carry a better prognosis than hose that are HPV negative; therefore, this is not an area in need of more research(Answer B is incorrect). Currently, HPV-16 status has not been evaluated as a predictor for response to any drug therapy option; neither has it been studied whethet pdministering the quadrivalent HPV vaccine can prevent disease recurrence if the patienl is HPV negative (Answer D is incorrect). It is not yet known whether the prophylactic vaccination of the population with quadrivalent vaccine will significant reduce the incidence of HPV-16-positive SCCHN (Answer C is incorrect). While important from an epidemiological perspective, for a pharmacist, using HPV status to recommend the best therapy for a patient is the most important area in need of more research (Answer A is correct).

questions.question: W.E. is eventually diagnosed with stage IVa carcinoma of the head and neck and is offered concurrent chemoradiation therapy with high-dose cisplatin every 3 weeks. His basic metabolic profile reveals a serum creatinine of 1.1 g/dL with estimated creatinine clearance of 35 mL/ min. Additionally, his hemoglobin is reported to be 8.8 g/dL platelet count is 313,000 cells/mm3, and absolute neutrophil count is 2700 cells/mm3,W.E. reports feeling overwhelmed and somewhat fatigued; his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is determined to be 2. Which one of the following treatment plans is most appropriate for W.E.?
options: A. Change high-dose cisplatin to low-dose cisplatin every 3 weeks.
B. Change cisplatin to carboplatin every 3 weeks.
D. Hold chemotherapy and reevaluate in I week.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. It is not appropriate to continue with cisplatin as prescribed given the patient's symptoms, anemia, and general condition (feeling overwhelmed) (Answer C is noorrect). Therefore, hold chemotherapy and reevaluate in I week is the best option(Answer D is correct). There is no evidence to support that changing from high- to lowdose cisplatin every 3 weeks will result in similar outcomes (Answer A is incorrect). If the patient had a better performance status, changing cisplatin to carboplatin every 3 weeks would be reasonable because of his decline in kidney function (Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following treatments is best for managing W.E.'s anemia?
options: A. Darbepoetin 200 mcg subcutaneously every 2 weeks.
B. Two units packed red blood cells.
C. Hold chemotherapy and administer intravenous hydration.
D. Erythropoietin alfa 10,000 units subcutaneously three times/week.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The best answer in this case is 2 units of packed red blood cells (Answer B is correct).Given the patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 and hemoglobin less than 10 g/dL, he requires treatment. Holding chemotherapy and administering intravenous hydration is not appropriate because hydration will not correct the anemia (Answer C is incorrect). Darbepoetin and epoetin alfa are not recommended in patients with head and neck cancer because of the increased mortality associated with their use when high hemoglobin concentrations are targeted (Answer A and Answer D are incorrect). In addition, it would take at least 4 weeks for the patient to experience a bemoglobin response. Given his current serum creatinine, estimated creatinine clearance,and age, the patient could be thought to have chronic renal insufficiency, in which case it might be argued that he is a candidate for an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA).However, the risks and benefits in head and neck cancer favor the use of red blood cell Iransfusion. The disease also has a significant impact on his daily activities, as shown by Ds performance status, which warrants more rapid correction of his anemia than an ESA would allow.

questions.question: A 58-year-old man presents with persistent stage Iva squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil and tongue. Six months ago, he was treated initially with 7 weeks of chemoradiation; the treatment course was complicated by the development of renal insufficiency with high dose cisplatin-based chemoradiation, and treatment was switched to cetuximab. He continued single-agent cetuximab for 2 months before developing persistent hypomagnesemia requiring intravenous magnesium replacement and grade 3 acneiform rash. Which one of the following is the most appropriate therapy for this patient's rash?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Oral clindamycin is the best option for treatment of the patient's grade 3 acneiform dermatitis, which is associated with cetuximab (Answer C is correct). Silver sulfadiazine I used for grade 2 radiation dermatitis and is not routinely employed in the treatment of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) rash (Answer A is incorrect).Metronidazole gel is used for grade 1 EGFR rash (Answer B is incorrect). Oral antihistamines like diphenhydramine are recommended for grade 2 EGFR rash (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 62-year-old man presents with a 3-month history of persistent sore throat and odynophagia. Biopsy reveals a stage 2 oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. The patient is on oxygen therapy for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and he takes furosemide, metoprolol, and lisinopril for congestive heart failure. He was treated 15 years ago for an early-stage rectal carcinoma with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery. His records indicate that he is often non-adherent to his medical appointments and that he tolerated only one of three planned cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.Which one of the following is the best treatment for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Radiation therapy alone is the best approach for this patient (Answer B is correct).Surgery is the preferred treatment approach for very small, localized, resectable oropharyngeal cancers; however, this patient is likely a high anesthesia risk given his oxygen-dependent chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure (Answer A is incorrect). Concurrent chemoradiation is the preferred treatment approach for localized oropharyngeal cancers, but he is not likely to tolerate or be adherent to his chemotherapy appointments, so chemoradiation is incorrect (Answer C is incorrect). Chemotherapy alone is incorrect because a local approach with either surgery or radiation is required for curative therapy for early-stage SCCHN (Answer D is incorrect). For localized oropharyngeal cancers, all of these are treatment options except for chemotherapy alone.

questions.question: Questions 120 and 121 pertain to the following case. G.G. is a 62-year-old man who presents for week 3 of daily external beam radiation therapy for stage III laryngeal carcinoma. He has complaints of dry mouth. Which one of the following is the most appropriate treatment option for G.G.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The most appropriate response is amifostine, supported by the American Society of Clinical Oncology treatment guidelines, and evidence supports prevention of xerostomia from radiation therapy for head and neck cancer (Answer C is correct). The evidence regarding the use of pilocarpine to treat xerostomia is inconsistent (Answer D is incorrect). Patient acceptance of saliva substitutes is poor (Answer A is incorrect).Palifermin has been studied only as a measure to reduce mucositis, not xerostomia(Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: On physical examination, G.G. is found to have several areas of inflamed sores in the radiation site. He also reports pain and soreness in this region. Which one of the following is the best approach to managing G.G.'s mucositis?
options: C. Bioadherent polyvinyI pyrrolidone, hyaluronic acid, and glycyrrhetinic acid gel.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The answer with the most evidence to support its use is the bioadherent oral gel (Answer C is correct). Although lidocaine, which is often used in clinical practice, would likely provide adequate local relief of the pain associated with mucositis, evidence to support its use is limited (Answer A is incorrect). If the patient reports more significant pain after a trial of local therapy with the bioadherent gel, lidocaine therapy may be the next step. Failing lidocaine therapy, opioid analgesics such as hydrocodone/acetaminophen might be employed to help the patient manage the pain (Answer B is incorrect).Palifermin has not consistently shown benefit for treating mucositis in this population(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 122 and 123 pertain to the following case. K.P. is a 31-year-old woman who presents to your wellness center to discuss cancer prevention. She is concerned about her risk of developing cervical cancer. Which one of the following is the best intervention for screening and prevention of cervical cancer for K.P.?
options: B. Pap smear and human papillomavirus (HPV) testing.
C. Pap smear and HPV vaccine.
D. Pap smear, HPV testing, and HPV vaccine.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Papanicolaou smear and HPV testing is the best answer because the patient is older than 30 (Answer B is correct). According to the American Congress of Obstetrics and Gynecology and American Cancer Society guidelines and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration-approved labeling, HPV testing should be conducted after age 30, and a Pap smear should be done at least once every 3 years. A Pap smear alone is incorrect because HPV testing is important to identify the patient's risk of developing cervical cancer (Answer A is incorrect). A Pap smear and HPV vaccine and a Pap smear, HPV testing, and HPV vaccine are both incorrect because the HPV vaccine is indicated for prevention, before HPV exposure in girls and women age 9-26. The patient is 31 and is a mother, confirming previous sexual activity and a high likelihood of previous exposure to HPV (Answer C and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: K.P. is also concerned about her risk of developing ovarian cancer. A greatgrandmother on her father's side died of ovarian cancer at the age of 72. K.P. had her first menstrual period at age 12. She currently takes no drug therapy or over-the-counter drugs. Her last pelvic examination, about I year ago, was normal. She is in general good health. Which one of the following is the best intervention for K.P. to reduce her risk of developing ovarian cancer?
options: A. Insert an intrauterine progesterone device.
B. Use oral contraceptives for at least 3 years.
C. Seek genetic screening to evaluate for hereditary risk.
D. Monitor cancer antigen (CA)-125 concentrations annually.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Oral contraceptives for at least 3 years is the best answer (Answer B is correct). Many clinical studies have shown the benefit of oral contraceptives in reducing the risk of ovarian cancer. These data support the incessant ovulation hypothesis that proposed ovulation is a hostile event. An intrauterine progesterone device is incorrect because progesterone, which does not influence ovulation, has not been shown to prevent ovarian cancer (Answer A is incorrect). Genetic screening to evaluate for hereditary risk is jncorrect because the patient has no hereditary risk factors (Answer C is incorrect)Although she had a great-grandmother with ovarian cancer, hereditary risk is associated with two or more first-degree relatives with ovarian cancer. An estimated 90% of ovarian cancer cases are sporadic. Monitoring cancer antigen (CA)-125 concentrations annually is not the best option (Answer D is incorrect). Although an elevated CA-125 concentration is a marker for ovarian cancer, it is a nonspecific marker of inflammation and could be elevated because of other benign abdominal conditions such as diarrhea of endometriosis. In addition, CA-125 is not always elevated in ovarian cancer.

questions.question: A 72-year-old woman has begun to experience new onset vaginal bleeding during the past 3 months. She is nulliparous and had her first menstrual period at age 10. She experienced menopause about I5 years ago, and she has been taking conjugated estrogen and progesterone once daily continuously since that time. She admits to often missing her progesterone doses. Which one of the following risk factors contributed the most to her suspected endometrial cancer?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Non-adherence to progesterone is the most likely risk factor for her suspected endometrial cancer (Answer C is correct). Unopposed estrogen therapy is associated with increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia, which increases risk of mutation and ultimately endometrial cancer. The purpose of progesterone in hormone regimens is to prevent endometrial hyperplasia. Lack of a pregnancy is a risk factor for ovarian cancer but is not associated with endometrial cancer (Answer A is incorrect). Use of hormone therapy decreased the risk of endometrial cancer in the Women's Health Study (Answer B is incorrect). However, long term hormone therapy is associated with increasing the risk of both breast and ovarian cancer. Her early menarche/ late menopause is not the best answer (Answer D is incorrect). Early menarche/late menopause is associated with increased lifetime exposure to hormones. However, for this woman, non-adherence to progesterone is contributes more than either early menarche or late menopause.

questions.question: A 64-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider with a 7-week history of constipation, fatigue, bloating, and early satiety. The preliminary computed tomography (CT) scan reveals a 5-cm x 5-cm localized abdominal mass. Which one of the following is the best approach to confirm a diagnosis in this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Surgery with staging is the best approach to confirm a diagnosis (Answer D is correct).During surgery, tumor samples can be obtained, and pathology can be completed to determine the diagnosis. Surgery is also the primary treatment intervention for this patient. Computed tomography-guided biopsy is not recommended because it is mnatomically difficult to accomplish without threat of microscopic seeding in the peritoneal cavity (Answer A is incorrect). Positron emission tomography is nol appropriate because it has not been established to be reproducible and predictive of diagnosis of ovarian cancer and most likely is not covered by insurance (Answer B is incorrect). The CA-125 plasma concentration, if elevated, is a marker for ovarian cancer,However, it is a nonspecific marker of inflammation and could be elevated because of Other benign abdominal conditions such as diarrhea or endometriosis. In addition, CAl25 is not always elevated in ovarian cancer (Answer C is incorrect),

questions.question: A 24-year-old woman (weight 76 kg, height 156 cm) is newly diagnosed with stage III cervical cancer. Her laboratory values are hemoglobin 12 g/dL, platelet count 156,000/mm3, absolute neutrophil count 2340/mm3, bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 1.1 mg/ dL by isotope dilution mass spectrometry (IDMS). Which one of the following is the best approach for primary treatment of this patient's newly diagnosed cervical cancer?
options: A. Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 weekly plus internal/external radiation.
B. Hysterectomy followed by adjuvant paclitaxel and carboplatin
C. Topotecan plus cisplatin followed by tumor reductive surgery.
D. Tumor reductive surgery followed by radiotherapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Cisplatin plus internal/external radiation is the best answer because this regimen has more than an 85% complete response/cure rate for patients with stage III advanced cervical cancer (Answer A is correct). Hysterectomy followed by adjuvant paclitaxel and carboplatin might be considered in a patient with stage I cervical cancer but has not had as much success with advanced disease (Answer B is incorrect). Topotecan plus cisplatin followed by tumor reductive surgery is incorrect because topotecan plus cisplatin is indicated for recurrent disease and did not shown any more efficacy than paclitaxel plus cisplatin in the Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) 2004 study(Answer C is incorrect). Tumor reductive surgery followed by radiotherapy might be considered if her disease were in an earlier stage or she had a major contraindication to chemotherapy; neither is the case for this woman (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: An 82-year-old woman (creatinine clearance, 41 mL/ minute), who has had no evidence of disease for 13 months, is seen today with her first recurrence of ovarian cancer. The oncologist states that she wants to treat the patient with platinum-based therapy. Which one of the following is the best regimen for the patient at this time?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Docetaxel plus carboplatin is the best option for this patient because she still has platinum/taxane sensitive disease as well as kidney dysfunction (Answer B is correct).Because patients with recurrent disease continue on chemotherapy indefinitely, it is important to adjust for organ dysfunction and identify treatment priorities. Liposomal doxorubicin plus carboplatin, gemcitabine plus carboplatin, and gemcitabine plus cisplatin are reasonable options but are least likely to be selected because of her kidney dysfunction (Answer A, Answer C, and Answer D are incorrect)). The goal would be to treat platinum-sensitive disease aggressively with a combination regimen while still minimizing risk of toxicity.

questions.question: Questions 128 and 129 pertain to the following case. L.J. is a 37-year-old woman with stage IIB recurrent ovarian cancer. At her clinic appointment to be cleared for this month's cycle of chemotherapy, she learns she has progressed on carboplatin treatment. Her CA-I25 is 75 U/mL. Her complete blood count is within normal limits, total bilirubin is 0.8 mg/dL, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is 28 U/L, and creatinine clearance is 35 mL/minute. Which one of the following is the best chemotherapy regimen for L.J. to receive for her next course of treatment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Docetaxel is the best treatment option because the dose does not need to be adjusted for kidney dysfunction (Answer D is correct). Both liposomal doxorubicin and gemcitabine should be used with caution (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect). Phase I studies of patients with ovarian cancer have shown increased toxicity in patients with kidney dysfunction, so dose adjustment is recommended. They are not the best options for this patient at this time. Topotecan is cleared by the kidneys; dose adjustments are recommended in the product information. Therefore, it is not the best option for the patient at this time (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Three months later, L.J. undergoes repeat CT scans, which suggest progression of disease with evidence of new liver implants, carcinomatosis, and increasing size of abdominal tumor. She also has new fluid accumulation in her peritoneal cavity. Her Jaboratory tests are CA-125 concentration 356 U/mL, hemoglobin 9 g/ dL, platelet count 103,000/mm3, and absolute neutrophil count 1600/mm3. Which one of the following is the best next chemotherapy option for L.J.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Cyclophosphamide and bevacizumab is the best regimen for this patient at this time on the basis of phase II study data that have shown improvement in progression-free survival (Answer A is correct). This regimen is well tolerated and has less associated toxicity than the other regimens listed. Although combination regimens of bevacizumab and topotecan or paclitaxel both have shown some benefit for treatment of recurrent ovarian cancer, because of this patient's clinical condition including borderline blood counts, significant tumor burden, and overall poor performance status, she is less likely to tolerate either regimen. Moreover, the topotecan dose should be reduced on the basis of her creatinine clearance of 35 mL/minute (Answer B and Answer C are incorrect).Bevacizumab is effective in recurrent ovarian cancer but is not as effective alone as when combined with cytotoxic agents (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 47-year-old woman has just completed six cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin adjuvant treatment of stage III optimally debulked ovarian cancer. She now has no evidence of disease, and her CA-125 concentration is 10 U/mL. Which one of the following is the best option to improve this patient's overall survival?
options: A. Consolidation chemotherapy with paclitaxel once a month for 12 cycles.
B. Continue paclitaxel and carboplatin once every 3 weeks for additional three cycles.
C. Monitor with CT scan and CA-125 concentration every 3 months.
D. Second-look surgery followed by chemotherapy if positive for residual disease.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Consolidation chemotherapy with paclitaxel is the best option for this patient because she has had a good response to her primary surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy with minimal residual toxicity (Answer A is correct). Because she is young, she should be treated aggressively. Based on GOG 178, 12 cycles of intravenous paclitaxel therapy improved progression-free survival, and final data suggested improved overall survival s well. An additional three cycles of paclitaxel plus carboplatin is reasonable and is often used when microscopic residual disease is suspected, which is evidenced by elevated CA-125. Because this patient has no evidence of disease and her CA-125 is within normal range, a "clinical complete response" can be declared. Therefore,continuing combination chemotherapy would not be best option and likely to only increase risk for cumulative toxicity (Answer B is incorrect). Clinical monitoring with CT scan and CA-125 concentration every 3 months is an acceptable option for a patient who has achieved a complete response to primary treatment; however, this now is considered a conservative approach and is less likely to be selected for a young patient(Answer C is incorrect). Second- look surgery, followed by chemotherapy if positive for residual disease, is controversial in clinical practice because no impact on overall survival has been shown in any clinical trial (Answer D is incorrect). This option might be selected on the basis of institutional bias toward second-look surgery for management of ovarian cancer.

questions.question: Questions 131 and 132 pertain to the following case. E.D. is a 72-year-old woman with recurrent papillary serous endometrial cancer. She had a hysterectomy followed by radiation and then six cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin.She achieved a complete response to her primary treatment and, for 2 years, has had no evidence of disease on surveillance. Today, she is told she has recurrent endometrial cancer. Which one of the following intravenous therapies is the best second-line treatment for E.D.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Paclitaxel and carboplatin is the best option for this patient because she responded so well to chemotherapy 2 years ago (Answer A is correct). Using the drugs that worked the first time to achieve a complete response is the best option. The other options are also reasonable but are not the best choices. Gemcitabine and cisplatin have activity in platinum-resistant endometrial cancer, so this option is reserved for platinum-resistant cancer (Answer B is incorrect). Although individually active, the combinations of doxorubicin and carboplatin and topotecan and cisplatin have not been formally evaluated for treatment of endometrial cancer (Answer C and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: E.D.'s endometrial cancer progresses through the treatment that was selected above. Which one of the following intravenous therapies is the best treatment for E.D.'s recurrent endometrial cancer?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Now that the patient has a platinum-resistant tumor, the combination of gemcitabine and cisplatin is the best option for her treatment because this regimen has demonstrated a more than 50% response rate in platinum-resistance endometrial cancer (Answer B is comrect). The combinations of cyclophosphamide and bevacizumab and doxorubicin and lopotecan have not been formally evaluated for treatment of platinum-resistant endometrial cancer (Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). Ifosfamide plus vincristine is not appropriate because she has a platinum- and/ or taxane-resistant tumor and this legimen has not been shown to have benefit in recurrent setting (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 57-year-old woman has stage IIl recurrent ovarian cancer. At her clinic appointment to be cleared to receive her chemotherapy, she learns she has progressed on carboplatin treatment. Her laboratory tests show: hemoglobin 11 g/dL, platelet count 123,000/ mm3, absolute neutrophil count 1600/mm3, creatinine clearance 75 mL/minute, total bilirubin 2.2 mg/dL, and AST 94 IU/L. Which one of the following is the best chemotherapy regimen for this patient's next course of treatment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Topotecan is the best option for this patient because it is eliminated renally, no dose adjustment is required, and no concerns exist about toxicity with liver dysfunction(Answer C is correct). Both liposomal doxorubicin and gemcitabine need to be used with Caution; phase I studies of patients with ovarian cancer have shown increased toxicity in patients with liver sufficiency, so dose adjustments are recommended. Therefore, these drugs are not the best option (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect). Docetaxel, which is eliminated primarily by the liver, should not be used when bilirubin is greater than 1.2 mg/dL. It could be used with significant dose adjustment, but it is not the best option at this time (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A professional women's networking group has invited you to speak at their September monthly meeting for Gynecologic Cancer Awareness month. The meeting will focus on endometrial cancer. Which one of the following prevention interventions is the most important for reducing the risk of endometrial cancer?
options: B. Participation in weight loss and exercise programs.
C. Participation in universal genetic screening programs.
D. Undergoing prophylactic hysterectomy after childbearing years.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Participation in weight loss and exercise programs is the best intervention for women wanting to reduce their risk of developing endometrial cancer because obesity is one of the risk factors with or without a family history (Answer B is correct). Avoidance of hormone therapy is not the best answer because hormone therapy has not been associated definitively with an increased risk of endometrial cancer (Answer A is incorrect). Participation in universal genetic screening programs is not the best intervention; it should be reserved for patients with a family history of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (Answer C is incorrect). Undergoing prophylactic hysterectomy after childbearing years, although preventive, is an aggressive intervention not supported by any clinical trial data. Not all women are at risk of developing endometrial cancer, and it can be detected and cured in early stages (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 40-year-old woman has newly diagnosed advanced endometrial cancer. She is not a surgical candidate because of her history of heart failure and type 2 diabetes. Her creatinine clearance is 95 mL/minute, total bilirubin is 1.1 mg/dL, and ALT is 18 U/L)In addition to cisplatin, which one of the following is the best regimen for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Paclitaxel plus cisplatin is the best option for this patient with newly diagnosed endometrial cancer, heart failure, and diabetes (Answer C is correct). Cisplatin is one of the most active drugs for the treatment of endometrial cancer, and the activity of the combination of paclitaxel plus cisplatin in endometrial cancer has been supported by the data from multiple phase II trials. Doxorubicin is contraindicated in patients with significant cardiac dysfunction, specifically heart failure (Answer A is incorrect).Gemcitabine with cisplatin is effective in recurrent, platinum-resistant endometrial cancer. It is not the best option because limited clinical data support its efficacy in newly diagnosed endometrial cancer (Answer B is incorrect). A lack of or limited clinical data is also the reason that docetaxel is not the best option for this patient. Docetaxel is often substituted for paclitaxel when unacceptable neuropathy occurs; however, this practice is based on clinical experience, not clinical trial data (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: An obese 32-year-old woman had her first menstrual period at age 9 but has had irregular menstrual cycles since age 15. She was recently given a diagnosis of polycystio ovarian syndrome. An aunt on her paternal side was given a diagnosis of ovarian cancer at the age of 67. The patient asks you for her lifetime risk of developing ovarian cancer.Which one of the following is the best screening option for ovarian cancer in this patient?
options: A. Annual pelvic examination, transvaginal ultrasonography, and CA-125 concentration.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. An annual pelvic examination is the best ovarian cancer screening option for this patient(Answer C is correct). Annual pelvic examination, transvaginal ultrasonography, and CA-125 concentration and genetic screening are appropriate for patients at high risk of developing ovarian cancer. Polycystic ovarian syndrome is associated with increased risk of endometrial cancer. She has no significant family history; her aunt is a seconddegree relative, and a familial risk is suspected when more than two first-degree relatives have been diagnosed with ovarian cancer (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect)Checking CA-125 concentrations every 6 months has limited benefit by itself because CA-125 is a nonspecific tumor marker and can be elevated in many benign conditions,including polycystic ovary syndrome, so it is not helpful in this patient (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 34-year-old woman with a history of stage IIb cervical cancer has just completed 5 weeks of external radiation with cisplatin once weekly followed by brachytherapy. She now has no evidence of disease. The patient is the mother of three children younger than 7 years. She would like aggressive treatment to prevent cancer recurrence. Which one of the following is the best plan after completion of chemotherapy and radiation treatment?
options: A. Six cycles of topotecan plus cisplatin.
B. Six cycles of paclitaxel plus carboplatin.
C. Follow-up examinations with a Pap smear every 3 months.
D. Total abdominal hysterectomy plus bilateral saipingo-oophorectomy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. A follow-up examination with a Pap smear every 3 months is the best monitoring plan for this patient (Answer C is correct). She has responded well to her primary chemoradiation. Although the patient is very concerned about risk of recurrence, no data support consolidation chemotherapy for cervical cancer. Therefore, although both six cycles of docetaxel with cisplatin and paclitaxel with cisplatin are effective chemotherapy regimens for the management of cervical cancer, it is not necessary or appropriate to continue chemotherapy at this time for this patient (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect). Total abdominal hysterectomy plus bilateral salpingooophorectomy, which addresses the role of secondary surgery after completion of chemoradiation, does not improve overall survival and has a high risk of morbidity and surgical complications because of operating in a recently radiated field (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 63-year-old woman presents with new-onset vaginal bleeding for I month. An endometrial biopsy confirms a new cancerous lesion. She undergoes total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with optimal tumor debulking surgery and receives a diagnosis of stage IIIA, high-grade endometrial cancer. Which one of the following is the best adjuvant approach for this patient to receive after surgery?
options: C. Six cycles of paclitaxel plus carboplatin.
D. External beam radiation plus cisplatin.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. External beam radiation plus cisplatin is the best option for adjuvant treatment because chemoradiation has more activity than chemotherapy alone to reduce risk of recurrence in patients with advanced (stage III) endometrial cancer (Answer D is correct). External adiation alone or six cycles of paclitaxel plus carboplatin might be considered, but in patients who can tolerate combined modalities, chemoradiation is prefered. It is likely tat she will get additional cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin after completion of cisplatin and radiation (Answer A and Answer C are incorrect). Follow-up examinations every 3 months might be considered in patients with many comorbidities or contraindications for radiation and chemotherapy. However, for her advanced disease and high risk of recurrence, adjuvant treatment should be offered (Answer B incorrect).

questions.question: A 64-year-old woman received a diagnosis of stage IIlb cancer of the ovary, She completed primary treatment with total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingooophorectomy and optimal debulking surgery followed by six cycles of intravenous paclitaxel plus intraperitoneal cisplatin. She now has no evidence of disease on her CT scan and her CA-125 concentration is 8 U/mL (357 U/mL at time of diagnosis). Her gynecologic oncologist tells her that she has achieved a complete response to het primary treatment. Which one of the following is the best next step to improve this patient's progression-free and overall survival?
options: A. Paclitaxel 135 mg/m2 intravenously every 4 weeks for 12 cycles.
B. Second-look surgery with peritoneal washings.
C. Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg every 21 days for 12 months.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Paclitaxel intravenously every 4 weeks for 12 cycles is the best next step for this woman(Answer A is correct). She received six cycles of paclitaxel intravenously with cisplatin intraperitoneally but not the intraperitoneal paclitaxel on day 8 that was used in the GOG I72 trial. The lack of intraperitoneal paclitaxel may affect her survival. This patient is at risk of recurrence similar to that seen with the intravenous regimen. The GOG 178 trial suggests that an additional 12 cycles of paclitaxel improves progression-free survival and may improve overall survival. Second-look surgery with peritoneal washings is controversial, and limited information is available in patients just completing Imtraperitoneal therapy; the risk of surgical complications may be high (Answer B is incorrect). Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg every 21 days for 12 months is not the best option until ongoing clinical studies are completed and more information is available (Answer C is incorrect). Having a follow-up examination every 3 months is not the best option;because she is young and otherwise healthy, aggressive treatment to prevent recurrence is the best option (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 141 and 142 pertain to the following case. G.W. is a 62-year-old man with a recent diagnosis of stage IV chronic lymphocytio leukemia/smali lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL). His white blood cell count (WBC)is 65,000/mm3,'hemoglobin is 11.9 g/dL, and platelet count is 120,000/mm3. A computed tomography scan revealed mediastinal and axillary lymphadenopathy. His bone marrow biopsy revealed 30% involvement by CLL/SLL. His medical history is unremarkable except for a history of chronic sinus infections for the past several months. Which one of the following therapies is the best choice to treat G.W.?
options: D. Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone (CHOP), and rituximab.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. For a patient with newly diagnosed CLL/SLL, treatment should be initiated because the patient has become symptomatic (chronic sinus infections). Fludarabine,cyclophosphamide, and rituximab is the most appropriate treatment at this time (Answet C is correct). According to National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines,a fludarabine-based regimen is appropriate in patients younger than 70 years.Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (CHOP) combined with rituximab is generally reserved for relapsed/refractory disease or patients with bulky lymphadenopathy (Answer D is incorrect). Although CHOP can be used as first-line treatment, it offers no survival advantage. Fludarabine may be appropriate for patients with significant comorbidities who are unable to tolerate intensive chemotherapy.However, given the patient's age and lack of comorbidities, a fludarabine-based combination regimen provides the most benefit in this situation (Answer A is incorrect).Ofatumumab is not the best choice; it is appropriate in relapsed disease that has failed Fludarabine and alemtuzumab (Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following therapies is the most appropriate second-line treatment for G.W.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Patients who have progressed after initial treatment can still have a good response to second-line treatments. In this case, given the lack of other comorbidities, the most appropriate option for this patient is bendamustine with rituximab, which has shown clear efficacy in patients in first relapse with overall response rates of 90% and complete response rates of 60% (Answer D is correct). Alemtuzumab offers only a 33% overall response rate in patients whose disease has failed fludarabine therapy (Answer A is incorrect). Although tositumomab has utility in low-grade/ indolent lymphomas, it does not have a role in patients with CLL/SLL (Answer B is incorrect). Chlorambucil is usually reserved for patients who may not tolerate more aggressive therapies (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 143 and 144 pertain to the following case. D.S. is a 52-year-old woman with newly diagnosed grade III follicular center cell lymphoma. Her WBC is 4200/mm3, hemoglobin is 12.5 g/dL, and platelet count is 120,000/ mm3. Her medical history is significant for arthritis, hypothyroidism, and diabetes mellitus. Which one of the following, in addition to rituximab, is the most appropriate first-line treatment for D.S?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The optimal treatment for this patient is CHOP in combination with rituximab (Answer C is correct). Although most follicular lymphomas are indolent, grade III follicular lymphomas behave more like diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. These patients need more aggressive treatment (e.g., CHOP in combination with rituximab). Neither CVP with rituximab nor fludarabine with rituximab are optimal choices; these treatments are appropriate for a grade I or II follicular lymphoma (Answer B and Answer D are incorrect). Bendamustine with rituximab should be reserved for relapsed or refractory low-grade lymphomas (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: Before initiation of chemotherapy, D.S.'s hepatitis B screen result comes back carrier positive. Additional laboratory work reveals an aspartate aminotransferase of 26 U/L and alanine aminotransferase of 20 U/L; she has no signs or symptoms of active hepatitis. Which one of the following is the most appropriate intervention for D.S.?
options: B. Discontinue rituximab and continue with chemotherapy.
C. Continue with rituximab and chemotherapy and monitor hepatic function.
D. Initiate treatment for hepatitis B and hold rituximab and chemotherapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Patients with a history of hepatitis B, but without active symptoms, may be able to receive rituximab and chemotherapy with monitoring of hepatic function(Answer C is correct). Reports of reactivation of hepatitis B and fulminant liver failure have led to changes in the package insert for rituximab. A rituximab dose reduction has not been shown to decrease the risk of reactivation (Answer A is incorrect). Discontinuing rituximab is not indicated unless the patient shows active symptoms of hepatitis reactivation (Answer B is incorrect). Holding rituximab and chemotherapy may be appropriate in a reactivation. Initiating antiviral therapy is not indicated in the absence of symptoms (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 145-147 pertain to the following case. C.D. is a 59-year-old man with newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma stage IIB. His WBC is 9800/mm3, hemoglobin is 10.9 g/dL, platelet count is 223,000/ mm3,and serum lactate dehydrogenase concentration is 1405 U/L. A computed tomography scan reveals several supraclavicular lymph nodes. His bone marrow biopsy shows no lymphoma involvement. His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypercholesterolemia. Which one of the following statements best describes C.D.'s prognosis?
options: A. Good risk and an estimated 4-year survival of 79%.
B. Low-intermediate risk and an estimated 5-year survival of 50%
C. High-intermediate risk and an estimated 5-year survival of 40%.
D. Poor risk and an estimated 4-year survival of 55%.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. According to the revised International Prognostic Index (IPI), this patient has one risk factor: elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase. This patient is younger than 60 years, has good performance status, has stage Il disease, and has no extranodal involvement. This places the patient in the good risk group, which carries a 79% 4-year survival rate (Answer A is correct). The revised IPI is more appropriate in this case because the patient will most likely receive a rituximab-based regimen. If the patient were older than 50 years, his IPI score would put him at a low-intermediate risk with an estimated 5-year survival of about 50% (Answer B is incorrect). Patients with three risk factors have a high intermediate risk and S-year survival of about 40% (Answer C is incorrect),whereas patients with three or more factors are poor risk and have an estimated 4-year survival of 55%(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following therapies is most appropriate for C.D.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The patient has a stage II diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with and an IPI score of 1. The patient's lymphoma is curable, and he has an excellent chance at long-term survival,Using CHOP with rituximab is the standard chemotherapy regimen for the treatment of aitfise large B-cell lymphoma and is the first choice in this case (Answer D is correct)Radioimmunotherapy is appropriate in low-grade lymphomas or in patients with transformed lymphomas (Answer B is incorrect). Bendamustine with rituximab is appropriate for relapsed or refractory low-grade lymphomas (Answer C is incorrect).Waichful waiting is not an appropriate choice for the patient with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: After 9 months of complete remission, C.D.'s lymphoma relapses. Which one of the following therapies is the best choice for C.D. at this time?
options: A. Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and dexamethasone (hyper-CVAD) with rituximab.
B. CHOP plus rituximab followed by autologous transplant.
C. Etoposide, methylprednisolone, cytarabine, cisplatin (ESHAP) with rituximab,
D. Ifosfamide, carboplatin, etoposide (ICE) with rituximab followed by autologous transplant.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The patient should receive ICE with rituximab followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (Answer D is correct). Patients with relapsed disease should receive chemotherapy to establish chemosensitivity and proceed to autologous stem cell transplantation. Etoposide, methylprednisolone, cytarabine, and cisplatin with rituximab is an appropriate salvage regimen; however, this patient should receive autologous stem cell transplantation afterward (Answer C is incorrect). Using CHOP with rituximab initially produced a complete remission in this patient. However, the short duration of remission and the risk of cardiotoxicity from cumulative anthracycline exposure make CHOP a poor choice for this patient (Answer B is incorrect). The hyper-CVAD regimen with rituximab is not the best choice because hyper-CVAD uses agents similar to CHOP and thus offers little benefit at this point (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 148-150 pertain to the following case. T.G. is a 30-year-old man with a diagnosis of grade II ollicular lymphoma. His oncologist will be initiating treatment with bendamustine and rituximab. Which one of the following patient education topics is most appropriate for T.G.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Both rituximab and bendamustine are associated with hypersensitivity reactions, and the patient should be counseled on this possibility (Answer B is correct). Cardiotoxicity is a Very low possibility with either drug (Answer A is incorrect). Cyclophosphamide, not pendamustine, has been associated with hemorrhagic cystitis (Answer C is incorrect);however, the incidence is extremely low and is more relevant in patients receiving high dose cyclophosphamide before stem cell transplantation. Pulmonary toxicity is not a common adverse effect with bendamustine or rituximab and is not relevant in this situation (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: T.G. is being evaluated before his third course of treatment. Today, he reports a severe erythematous rash that has developed since his last treatment. Which one of the following is the most appropriate next course of action?
options: A. Administer hydrocortisone before next treatment.
B. Initiate doxycycline and proceed with therapy.
C. Hold rituximab and proceed with bendamustine.
D. Switch to an alternative chemotherapy regimen.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The patient has a low-grade lymphoma that is responsive to treatment, although not curable. The best answer is to switch to an alternative treatment regimen (Answer D is Correct). Patients with severe cutaneous reactions associated with bendamustine can develop toxic epidermal necrolysis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Premedication with hydrocortisone might alleviate a rituximab reaction, but it would not provide much benefit in a cutaneous reaction to bendamustine (Answer A is incorrect). Doxycycline has shown benefit in tyrosine kinase inhibitor-induced rashes, but no data have been reported with bendamustine-induced rashes (Answer B is incorrect). Discontinuing rituximab would likely provide little benefit because the skin reaction is most likely caused by bendamustine (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: After six courses of chemotherapy, T.G. is now in complete remission. Which one of the following is the most appropriate course of action for this patient?
options: C. Consolidate with localized radiation therapy.
D. Proceed to stem cell transplant.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Patients with follicular lymphoma in first remission should receive rituximab maintenance (Answer B is correct). Clinical trials have shown improved progression free Survival in patients who receive maintenance rituximab compared with those who did not. Continued follow-up and monitoring may be appropriate in some circumstances,such as for a patient who has significant comorbidities or who is unable to tolerate rituximab (Answer A is incorrect). Consolidation with radiation therapy is occasionally used in patients with residual masses or in patients with aggressive lymphomas who present with bulky lymphadenopathy (Answer C is incorrect). Patients who have relapsed and achieved a second remission should proceed to transplantation. However,this patient is in first remission and may still have a prolonged progression-free survival(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 151 and 153 pertain to the following case. S.D. is a 63-year-old woman with a newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma Her WBC is 8600/mm3, hemoglobin is 10.3 g/dL, platelet count is 223,000/mm3, and serum lactate dehydrogenase concentration is 1844 U/L. A computed tomography scan reveals multiple axillary, retroperitoneal, and pelvic lymphadenopathies. Her bone marrow biopsy shows no lymphoma involvement. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and breast cancer previously treated with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide for six cycles. She complains of increasing fatigue over the last 2 months, and recent echocardiography revealed an ejection fraction of 30%. In addition to rituximab, which one of the following regimens is most appropriate for S.D.?
options: A. CVP followed by autologous transplant.
D. Bendamustine followed by autologous transplant.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The most appropriate treatment choice for this patient at this point is ESHAP with rituximab (Answer C is correct). Treatment with CVP with rituximab is inadequate for a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Answer A is incorrect). Although CHOP with rituximab is the standard treatment regimen for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma,because of the patient's decreased ejection fraction, anthracyclines should be avoided(Answer B is incorrect). Bendamustine with rituximab has not been adequately studied in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Answer D is incorrect). The patient should only receive bendamustine and rituximab in the context of a clinical trial.

questions.question: During the initial treatment, S.D. develops chills and rigors thought to be related to her infusion. Which one of the following is the most appropriate course of action during subsequent infusions for her infusion-related adverse reactions?
options: D. Continue rituximab using a rapid infusion rate.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Infusion-related reactions are common during the initial infusion of rituximab.Subsequent infusions are much better tolerated, and a rapid rate infusion is appropriate if a patient does not have a grade 3 or 4 infusion reaction (Answer D is correct).Discontinuation of rituximab is not warranted because the patient did not have a hypersensitivity reaction (Answer A is incorrect). A rate reduction may be indicated in patients with a grade 3 or 4 infusion reaction (Answer C is incorrect). A dose reduction has not been shown to alter the incidence of infusion reactions and is not appropriate(Answer B is incorrect).

questions.question: A 67-year-old man has a history of CLL/SLL originally diagnosed in 2006. Today,his WBC is 53,000/mm3, hemoglobin is 11.9 g/dL, and platelet count is 82,000/ mm3.
