A computed tomography scan reveals negligible lymphadenopathy. A bone marrow biopsy reveals 30% involvement by CLL. His medical history is unremarkable except for respiratory infections for the past several months. He has been treated in the past with CVP plus rituximab and a fludarabine-based regimen. Which one of the following agents is most appropriate to treat this patient's CLL/SLL?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Although all agents are indicated for the treatment of relapsed CLL, alemtuzumab is the best choice for this patient because of the bone marrow involvement and minimal lymphadenopathies (Answer B is correct). Ibritumomab is incorrect; it is an appropriate choice for a patient with minimal bone marrow involvement and extensive lymphadenopathies (Answer A is incorrect). Likewise, chlorambucil may be used for the treatment of CLL; however, several other regimens have better response rates (Answer C is incorrect). Ofatumumab is indicated for patients whose disease has failed fludarabine and alemtuzumab (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 154-157 pertain to the following case. J.W. is a 27-year-old man with a newly diagnosed Burkitt lymphoma. His laboratory values include a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL, total bilirubin of 1.4 mg/dL, and lactate dehydrogenase concentration of 2100 U/L. His medical history is significant for HIV,and his current CD4 count is 44/mm3. Which one of the following is the best treatment option for J.W.?
options: A. Initiate highly active antiretroviral treatment and chemotherapy.
B. Start chemotherapy and initiate highly active antiretroviral treatment once remission is achieved.
C. Initiate highly active antiretroviral treatment and start chemotherapy once the CD4 count normalizes.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. This patient should be treated with highly active antiretroviral therapy and chemotherapy gimultaneously (Answer A is correct). Clinical trials have shown that patients with AIDS can be safely and effectively treated with chemotherapy and antiretroviral drugs simultaneously and have improved responses compared with chemotherapy alone. On the basis of this same evidence, starting chemotherapy and initiating highly active antiretroviral treatment once remission is achieved is incorrect (Answer B is incorrect),The patient has a highly aggressive lymphoma and requires treatment urgently; thus,highly active antiretroviral therapy alone is inappropriate (Answer C is incorrect). An Butologous transplantation may be an option once the disease responds to treatment, but Combination chemotherapy with antiretroviral therapy must be initiated before consideration for transplantation (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following chemotherapeutic options is the best intervention for J.W.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The best chemotherapeutic option for this patient is hyper-CVAD (Answer C is correcti).The CHOP chemotherapy option, with or without rituximab, is inadequate for patients wih Burkitt lymphoma (Answer A and Answer B are incorrect). The addition of inximab may be warranted in patients with an adequate CD4 count. However, this patienr's CD4 count of 44/mm3 precludes the use of rituximab with hyper-CVAD at this point (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: J.W, is about to receive his first course of chemotherapy. Which one of the following is the most relevant in educating the patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Vincristine causes peripheral neuropathies, and the patient should be educated on this adverse effect and informed to notify his provider if he exhibits these symptoms(Answer D is correct). Cyclophosphamide has been associated with hemorrhagic eystitis, however, the incidence is extremely low and is more relevant in patients receiving high-dose cyclophosphamide with stem cell transplantation (Answer C is incoreet). Hand-foot syndrome is occasionally seen with a variety of cytotoxic agents.However, standard doxorubicin is not known to cause hand-foot syndrome (Answer B is incomec). Venoocclusive disease is an important adverse effect that can be seen in patients receiving stem cell transplants. However, at this point in the patient's treatment,he risk of venoocclusive disease is minimal (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: J.W.'s hematologist is considering initiating central nervous system prophylaxis,Together with systemic chemotherapy, which one of the following prophylactie strategies is most appropriate for J.W.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Pabents with Burkitt lymphoma are at high risk of developing central nervous system involvement. If prophylaxis is not given, 30% to 50% of patients develop central peryous system relapse. Therefore, central nervous system monitoring is incorrect(Answer A is incorrect). Intrathecal chemotherapy, together with systemic chemotherapy, is the most appropriate course of action for this patient (Answer C is Morrect). Central nervous system prophylaxis with intrathecal chemotherapy has decreased the incidence of isolated central nervous system relapse and has improved long-term survival. Although spinal and whole brain radiation have been used in the Past, radiation does not improve outcomes over the combination of systemic and ltrathecal chemotherapy (Answer B is incorrect). In addition, combining radiation and intrathecal chemotherapy with systemic chemotherapy has resulted in long-term complications and severe neurotoxicity (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 158-160 pertain to the following case. H.A. is a 68-year-old woman recently received a diagnosis of stage II CLL/SLL. Her WBC is 65,000/mm3, hemoglobin is 12.5 g/dL, and platelet count is 120,000/mm3. A computed tomography scan reveals axillary lymphadenopathies. Her bone marrow biopsy reveals 20% involvement by CLL/SLL. Her medical history is significant for obesity, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension, but she has no other complaints. Which one of the following treatment options is best for this patient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The patient is given a diagnosis of stage II SLL/CLL. Based on the information available, her disease appears to be indolent with low-risk features. Although she has an elevated white blood cell count, she does not have any active symptoms of disease at this time. Given the lack of symptoms, weakness, painful lymphadenopathy, symptomatic anemia and/or thrombocytopenia, recurrent infections, or rapidly progressive disease,watchful waiting is an appropriate option for the patient (Answer A is correct).Rituximab and chlorambucil are appropriate options for a patient with rapidly progressive disease who is not a candidate for more intense chemotherapy (Answer B and Answer D are incorrect). Bendamustine and rituximab may also be used in a patient who is able to tolerate chemotherapy, but none of these regimens shows improved overall survival (OS)(Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following best describes H.A.'s prognosis?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. According to the follicular lymphoma international prognostic index, this patient has a high-risk follicular lymphoma and an estimated 10-year OS of 35.5% (Answer D is correct). Her prognostic score is based on her age, hemoglobin concentration, and stage.Patients with a low risk follicular lymphoma have a much better prognosis and an estimated 5-year OS of 90% (Answer A is incorrect) and 10-year OS of 70%. If this patient had only two risk factors, her disease would be classified as intermediate risk with an estimated 10-year OS of 50% (Answer B is incorrect) and 5-year OS of 75%(Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the most appropriate treatment strategy for H.A.?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. This patient has a poor-risk follicular lymphoma, and treatment should be initiated.Although all four choices have been used in the first-line treatment of follicular lymphoma, CVP and rituximab is the most acceptable choice (Answer B is correct).Clinical trials have shown that alemtuzumab has efficacy in CLL, but its efficacy in follicular lymphoma has not been evaluated. Fludarabine has been evaluated as first-line therapy in follicular lymphoma, but only in combination with other cytotoxic agents(Answer C is incorrect). Single-agent fludarabine may be appropriate in patients who are elderly or not candidates for aggressive chemotherapy. Tositumomab is contraindicated because of the significant presence of lymphoma in the patient's bone marrow (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 58-year-old man presents to the stem cell transplant clinic for evaluation. His history includes acute myeloid leukemia, initially treated with standard dose chemotherapy in 2005 because of his good risk prognosis based on cytogenetics.Because he has since relapsed, he was re-induced with standard chemotherapy. His siblings are currently being processed for a possible donor match. It is determined that the patient will receive busulfan and cyclophosphamide as high-dose chemotherapy with methotrexate and cyclosporine as graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis.According to institutional protocol, the patient will receive prophylactic posaconazole,acyclovir, and ciprofloxacin. When he is discharged after an allogeneic transplant,which one of the following is the most important counseling point?
options: A. Long-term acyclovir is required to prevent viral infections as the lymphocyte count recovers.
B. Posaconazole and ciprofloxacin can both prolong the QTc interval, and electrocardiographic monitoring is required.
C. Adherence to GVHD prophylaxis and follow-up to assess drug concentrations are important.
D. Checking blood pressure at home is recommended because cyclosporine can increase the blood pressure.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. For patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) for acute myeloid leukemia, an allogeneic transplantation provides the greatest potential for graft.versus-leukemia effect. However, GVHD is a potentially serious life-threatening adverse event. Immunosuppression is the mainstay of preventing GVDH and requires frequent drug concentration monitoring for efficacy and toxicity (Answer C is correct). Acyciovir prophylaxis is warranted for the prevention of herpes viral infections; however, this is not the most life threatening complication after high dose chemotherapy and transplantation (Answer A is incorrect). Posaconazole and ciprofloxacin have the potential to prolong QTc, and any bradycardia would require an electrocardiographig ponitoring, but this is not the most serious counseling point (Answer B is incorrect).Blood pressure monitoring is important with calcineurin use, but not as important as adherence to the therapy and monitoring of levels (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 45-year-old woman has received six cycles of standard therapy for non-Hodgkin diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She has a relapse 14 months after her last dose of chemotherapy. The plan is to treat her with high-dose carmustine, etoposide, cytarabine,and melphalan. Which of the following reasons is most important for using highdose chemotherapy?
options: A. The lymphoma is deemed chemosensitive.
B. The lymphoma is deemed resistant to conventional dose chemotherapy.
C. The patient relapsed after 12 months.
D. It is used as consolidation therapy following standard induction chemotherapy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Transplantation may be considered second-line therapy with curative intent in patients who relapse after 9 months of initial therapy with continued chemosensitivity (Answer C is correct). For a patient with relapsed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, assessing chemosensitivity before transplantation is a priority because those without sensitive disease even with an early relapse are unlikely to benefit even from the high doses of a preparative regimen (Answer A is incorrect). If a patient derives at least a partial response to chemotherapy, then proceeding to high-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation is the standard of care for relapsed disease. Patients with chemoresistant disease may respond to high-dose chemotherapy initially, but rsponses are not durable (Answer B is incorrect). The use of consolidation with highdose chemotherapy is not of any proven benefit after initial therapy and should be neserved for relapsed disease (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A 26-year-old man with relapsed testicular cancer is being treated and monitored as an outpatient. He is currently 2 days into his high-dose carboplatin and etoposide chemotherapy and will be receiving his stem cells in 3 days. He is also receiving antimicrobial prophylaxis with levofloxacin, vancomycin, and acyclovir. He can take oxycodone for pain and lorazepam for nausea. The patient comes to the outpatient clinic daily for chemotherapy, antimicrobial drugs, daily laboratory tests, and for 3 liters of intravenous fluid. Which one of the following is the most important monitoring parameter to educate this patient on?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Carboplatin and etoposide followed by an autologous stem cell rescue in a tandem fashion is the standard of care for relapsed germ cell tumors and may provide a 60%cure rate as second-line therapy. When transplant occurs, patients will be seen daily in the outpatient clinic; they will require substantial education about life-threatening situations during the transplant process. The most life threatening situation would be bleeding and infection. An elevated temperature should be taken as an infection until proven otherwise and require immediate admission with intravenous antibiotics (Answer Ais comect). Monitoring of urine output, blood pressure, and symptoms of mucositis are routine during outpatient monitoring and patient education, but are not the most life hreatening (Answer B, Answer C, and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 164-166 pertain to the following case. W.F. is a 21-year-old man with mature B-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia. Now in his second remission, he is being typed for allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation(HCT). Which of the following donors would provide W.F. with the best match for HCT?
options: A. A brother with a full human leukocyte antigen (HLA) match.
B. A sister with a full HLA match.
D. Umbilical cord donor matched at A, B, and C.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The least likely chance of developing acute GVHD is receiving an HCT from a fully Ielated sibling at the major histocompatibility sites. This patient is also more likely to match at minor histocompatibility sites if he received stem cells from a sibling; with preference given to a male donor (Answer A is correct). A brother takes precedence over I sister; especially if the sister has a history of pregnancy (Answer B is incorrect),Historically, matched unrelated donors carry a higher risk of GVHD, although novel buman leukocyte antigen (HLA) matching technology is quickly closing the difference i outcomes (Answer C is incorrect). Having a fully matched related donor supersedes ubilical cord transplantation (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: W.F. proceeded to transplantation and received conditioning chemotherapy with busulfan plus cyclophosphamide as his preparative regimen. He is now receiving tacrolimus 0.02 mg/kg and methotrexate as GVHD prophylaxis. Which one of the following combinations would provide the best monitoring parameters for W.F.'s immunosuppressant drugs?
options: B. Serum creatinine, hepatic panel, potassium, magnesium.
D. White blood cell count, platelets, hemoglobin.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The dose-limiting toxicity of tacrolimus is nephrotoxicity, which requires stringent monitoring. Electrolyte disturbances can also occur because of electrolyte wasting;byperkalemia can develop with acute kidney failure. In addition to nephrotoxicity,Methotrexate and tacrolimus can result in hepatotoxicity (Answer B is correct). Lipid panel should be monitored in patients with a history of coronary artery disease or diabetes but is not routine for patients on immunosuppression (Answer A is incorrect)Cardiac monitoring is required for patients receiving cyclophosphamide, but routine monitoring is not required in patients receiving calcineurin prophylaxis (Answer C is incorrect). Complete blood cell counts are monitored daily during hospitalization for transfusion requirements, but they are not necessarily required for immunosuppression(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: W.F.'s total bilirubin on day +15 is 2 mg/dL and increases to 4 mg/dL by day +21.He has also gained 7.2 kg since admission and has increasing right-sided abdominal pain. Hepatic enzymes remain normal and he has no nausea or diarrhea. Which one of the following is the best explanation for W.F.'s symptoms?
options: A. Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS) from busulfan.
B. Hepatosplenic candidiasis from prolonged neutropenia.
D. Acute GVHD of the liver.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Sinusoidal obstructive syndrome from busulfan is a serious and life-threatening complication after an allogeneic HCT and presents with increasing bilirubin, weight gain, and hepatic ascites (Answer A is correct). Risk factor include unrelated stem cell Source, history of hepatic injury, advanced age of transplant recipient, pretransplant exposure to gemtuzumab ozogamicin, and busulfan-containing preparative regimens.Hepatosplenic candidiasis from prolonged neutropenia is possible; however, blood cultures are negative, and disease progression with previous exposure to busulfan is more compatible with SOS (Answer B is incorrect). Although methotrexate can cause hepatotoxicity, it is unlikely to result in substantial weight gain and reversal of hepatic blood flow (Answer C is incorrect). Acute GVHD of the liver is incorrect because of the temporal relationship; occurring near day +21 (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A patient is receiving methotrexate and tacrolimus for GVHD prophylaxis after an allogeneic HCT for acute lymphocytic leukemia. Serum creatinine increases from 0.8 to 1.6 mg/dL on day +11, with a 2-L decrease in urine output over 24 hours. He also develops grade IV mucositis from his preparative regimen. This morning, his tacrolimus concentration was 35 ng/mL. Which of the following regimen changes would be best for this patient?
options: B. Discontinue methotrexate and continue tacrolimus with a 25% dose reduction
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Nephrotoxicity secondary to tacrolimus or methotrexate is a consequence that may lead to increased morbidity and mortality during the transplant process. Calcineurin associated nephrotoxicity can cause acute tubular necrosis by reductions in renal blood flow from reduced production of vasodilators and enhanced release of vasoconstrictors.Discontinuing tacrolimus and methotrexate because of the development of acute nephrotoxicity and mucositis is reasonable because the patient will have difficulty eliminating the methotrexate, which will lead to worsening mucositis (Answer A is correct). Although calcineurin associated nephrotoxicity is common after transplantation, a recommendation to reduce the dose by 25% is inappropriate because the blood level is already supra-therapeutic at 35 ng/mL, which necessitates holding the dose (Answer B is incorrect). Discontinue tacrolimus and discontinuing methotrexate are incorrect because both agents should be held rather than used as single agents (Answer C and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 168-170 pertain to the following case. M.R. is a 29-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia undergoing a matched unrelated donor (MUD) allogeneic HCT. Her preparative regimen consisted of totnl body irradiation/cyclophosphamide/etoposide, and her immunosuppression was mabbit antithymocyte globulin for three doses, sirolimus, and tacrolimus. M.R. has high-risk acute myeloid leukemia based on cytogenetic abnormalities and has previously received induction chemotherapy. She has just finished her first cycle of consolidation chemotherapy. She is receiving prophylaxis with ciprofloxacin, fluconazole, and acyclovir. She is found to be in a complete remission. Which one of the following best reflects the expected outcome of M.R.'s treatment compared with an autologous transplant?
options: A. Increased chance of long-term survival.
B. Increased chance of disease-free survival.
C. Less chance of long-term side effects.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Patients with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia who have intermediate- or high-risk cytogenetics and who attain a complete remission after induction chemotherapy are more likely to have long-term survival with an allogeneic HCT than with further standard dose chemotherapy administered as consolidation, as shown in a recent metaanalysis (Answer A is correct). The patient also has the benefit of young age, which is associated with lower treatment related mortality. Autologous transplant may have less long term adverse events because of the lack of potential GVHD and risk of fungal or viral infections, but it will not afford the patient a significant survival benefit (Answer B,Answer C, and Answer D are incorrect). Autologous transplant is as effective as further conventional chemotherapy, presumably because of the risk of leukemia contamination, and is less likely to have increased disease-free survival.

questions.question: On day +5, M.R. develops a fever, widespread rash, itching, arthralgia, and malaise.Vital signs are temperature 100.4°F (38°C), heart rate 80 beats/minute, blood pressure 100/78 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 16 breaths/minute. Which one of the following therapies is the most likely causative agent?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The patient is receiving a matched unrelated donor and is receiving antithymocyte globulin as part of her GVHD prophylaxis. Because the product is from a nonhuman gource, anaphylaxis and allergic reactions may occur. This patient is experiencing serum yickness; making antithymocyte globulin the correct choice (Answer C is correct).Etoposide,fluconazole, and ciprofloxacin may all cause a rash but not the allergic reactions described as serum sickness (Answer A, Answer B, and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: On day +85, M.R. develops 1.8 L of diarrhea/day, abdominal cramping, and rash covering 50% of her body; she is admitted to the stem cell transplantation floor. Her drugs include: ciprofloxacin 500 mg by mouth two times/day, fluconazole 400 mg intravenously daily, acyclovir 800 mg intravenously two times/day, tacrolimus 0.5 mg continuous intravenous infusion, sirolimus 3 mg daily, and amlodipine 10 mg daily. She has been treated with high-dose methylprednisolone, and her current taper dose is 80 mg once daily. Which one of the following changes in antimicrobial prophylaxis is the most appropriate for M.R.?
options: A. Change ciprofloxacin to metronidazole 500 mg three times/day.
B. Change acyclovir to valganciclovir 900 mg two times/day.
C. Change fluconazole to micafungin 100 mg intravenously daily.
D. Change fluconazole to posaconazole 200 mg three times/day.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. This patient has a diagnosis consistent with clinical grade III acute GVHD with skin and pastrointestinal involvement. Initiation of methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day is the standard of care. A change from fluconazole to posaconazole (Answer D is correct) or voriconazole, not micafungin (Answer C is incorrect), is recommended to provide antimold coverage because use of high-dose steroids after an allogeneic HCT increases the risk of an Aspergillus infection. Without a positive Clostridium difficile culture,ciprofloxacin should not be changed to metronidazole (Answer A is incorrect). A biopsy should be sent to look for cytomegalovirus inclusions; however, a rash would not be present with this type of viral infection, and GVHD is more likely; therefore, changing acyclovir to valganciclovir is incorrect (Answer B is incorrect). In addition,valganciclovir prophylaxis is inappropriate because routine plasma monitoring for cytomegalovirus would lead to preemptive therapy, rather than prophylaxis.

questions.question: Which one of the following is most likely to be considered a contraindication to the continued use of methotrexate for GVHD prophylaxis?
options: C. Estimated creatinine clearance less than 50 mL/min.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Third spacing in situations such as ascites or pleural effusions can lead to the accumulation of drug and delayed elimination, so patients with these conditions should not receive methotrexate (Answer A is correct). Although methotrexate can worsen mucositis, it is more appropriate to hold or discontinue it with grade IV rather than grade I mucositis (Answer B is incorrect). Estimated creatinine clearance less than 50 mL/minute is incorrect because patients with stage III kidney disease can still eliminate the drug (Answer C is incorrect). However, if acute kidney failure occurs, then discontinuing methotrexate is appropriate. Posaconazole interferes with the metabolism and elimination of calcineurin inhibitors but not methotrexate (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: A patient who is 89 days after an allogeneic HCT develops bloody diarrhea of 8 L/day. A desquamating rash covers 100% of her body. A confirmed biopsy reveals newly diagnosed GVHD. Which one of the following is the most appropriate treatment option for this patient?
options: C. Antithymocyte globulin 2.5 mg/kg daily for 3 days.
D. Infliximab i0 mg/kg weekly for 4 weeks.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Corticosteroids are the mainstay for the treatment of acute GVHD, with Methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day being the initial choice (Answer A is correct).Infliximab is incorrect; it is appropriate as second-line therapy because tumor necrosis factor inhibitors induce response in patients who have acute GVHD refractory to Corticosteroids (Answer D is incorrect). Although the addition of mycophenolate is Promising given the results of a phase II trial, it requires validation in a phase III study(Answer B is incorrect). Antithymocyte globulin is inappropriate; it is used for prophylaxis and as a second-line treatment option for acute GVHD because of increased risk of fungal infections when corticosteroids are used as first-line treatment (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A patient with multiple myeloma received only a partial response with her autologous transplantation 2 months ago. The transplantation was complicated because of prolonged difficulty swallowing and painful bloody ulcerations in her upper gastrointestinal tract. Her attending physician decides that the patient would benefit from a second transplantation with melphalan 140 mg/m2 plus total body irradiation. Which one of the following would most likely aid in preventing the previous complications this patient experienced?
options: B. Reduce the dose of melphalan.
C. Avoid the use of methotrexate for GVHD prophylaxis.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Because the patient had a previous complication of grade IV severe mucositis,palifermin is an appropriate prophylactic agent (Answer D is correct). It reduces the incidence and duration of severe mucositis with total body irradiation- containing conditioning regimens. Patient-controlled analgesia as preemptive therapy is incorrect because data do not support the use of opioids in patients without pain (Answer A is incorrect). Reducing the melphalan dose is incorrect because it is the main effective therapy against the myeloma (Answer B is incorrect). Avoiding methotrexate, which can cause mucositis, is incorrect because with autologous stem cell transplantation, the patient will not receive GVHD prophylaxis with methotrexate (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: Which one of the following is most important to discuss for the prevention of early infection after the preparative regimen until neutrophil recovery?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Antibacterial prophylaxis with ciprofloxacin should be strongly considered for patients undergoing an HCT with anticipated neutropenic episodes longer than 7 days secondary to a reduction in mortality from gram negative pathogens (Answer A is correct).Gatifloxacin has been studied in this patient population and has less gram-negative coverage (required because of the gastrointestinal tract irritation secondary to chemotherapy and radiation) compared with ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin (Answer B is incorrect). Intravenous immune globulin should not be routinely administered unless the patient has severe hypogammaglobulinemia (Answer C is incorrect). Vancomycin is inappropriate because the lack of benefit outweighs the risk of the emergence of resistant microorganisms (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Which of the following is most important to discuss when counseling patients on long-term complications/toxicities for survivors of highdose chemotherapy for germ cell tumors?
options: D. Increased risk of bladder cancer.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Patients undergoing high-dose chemotherapy for germ cell tumors should receive carboplatin 700 mg/ m2 and etoposide 750 mg/m2 daily for 3 days. High-dose carboplatin, together with previous cisplatin exposure, can increase the rate of peripheral neuropathy, usually in a stocking-and-glove distribution, which may persist even after chemotherapy has finished (Answer C is correct). Shortness of breath/pneumonitis may occur because of over hydration, but it is not a long-term complication from the drugs usually used for high-dose chemotherapy of germ cell tumors (Answer A is incorrect)Transient hepatitis may occur with etoposide, but liver enzymes normalize without long term sequelae (Answer B is incorrect). Secondary malignancies such as bladder cancer are more common with allogeneic stem cell transplantation and are not common in patients with germ cell malignancies undergoing an autologous transplantation (Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: Questions 176 and 177 pertain to the following case. R.A. is a 58-year-old man who received a diagnosis of multiple myeloma 6 months ago when he fractured his femoral head in a fall. His medical history is significant for a deep venous thrombosis and hypertension. He has been undergoing treatment with lenalidomide 25 mg orally daily and dexamethasone 40 mg every Monday for 6 months.His disease has shown a complete response, with disappearance of free light chains since therapy initiation. Which one of the following treatments is the most appropriate for R.A.'s multiple myeloma?
options: A. Melphalan 100 mg/m2 plus total body irradiation followed by allogeneic stem cell rescue.
B. Melphalan 200 mg/m2 followed by autologous stem cell rescue.
C. Continue lenalidomide and dexamethasone and add melphalan 200 mg/m2.
D. Melphalan 16 mg/m2 plus lenalidomide followed by an autologous stem cell transplantation.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. When a patient younger than 65 years with multiple myeloma attains a response with induction chemotherapy or immunomodulating agents, the treatment of choice is rescue to provide a more prolonged disease-free survival (Answer B is correct). Melphalan 100 mg/m2 plus total body irradiation followed by allogeneic stem cell rescue is incorrect because the melphalan dose is too low (Answer A is incorrect). Continued treatment with lenalidomide plus dexamethasone is incorrect because event-free and OS are poorer compared with that of high-dose melphalan (Answer C is incorrect). Melphalan plus lenalidomide is incorrect because of lack of supporting data, although trials are ongoing(Answer D is incorrect).

questions.question: R.A. proceeds to stem cell collection with filgrastim 10 mcg/kg subcutaneously daily for 4 days, followed by an apheresis collection. Which one of the following would best optimize collection for this patient?
options: C. Add plerixafor 0.24 mg/kg starting the night of the fourth day.
D. Split the filgrastim dose to two times/day.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. More than 4 months of lenalidomide use is a known risk factor for poor stem cell mobilization. Adding plerixafor to filgrastim increases collection potential as initial therapy and in patients who have not responded to filgrastim monotherapy stem cell mobilization (Answer C is correct). Plerixafor is given as a single subcutaneous injection the evening before stem cell collection. Splitting the filgrastim dose or are inappropriate because these two options offer limited to no advantage over this patient's current dose of filgrastim changing to sargramostim (Answer D and Answer B are incorrect).Cyclophosphamide plus filgrastim is a potentially effective chemomobilization regimen for patients requiring stem cell mobilization initially or as salvage therapy. However,this regimen requires admission to the hospital with hyperhydration and mesna uministration followed by a 10- to 14-day recovery period. Because the patient is arady in the process of mobilization, the administration of plerixafor would result in more convenience and less toxicity for him (Answer A is incorrect).

questions.question: You are providing care to a patient who has engraft 14 days after his stem cell reinfusion and who will be discharged tomorrow. He has been receiving lorazepam I mg two times/day for nausea and oxycodone 10 mg two times/day for resolving mucositis.His laboratory values, which have been stable over the last 3 days, are: sodium 132 mEq/L, potassium 2.9 mEq/L, chloride 112 mEq/L, serum bicarbonate 18 mEq/L, BUN 22 mg/dL, SCr 0.9 mg/dL, serum glucose 125 mg/dL, total serum calcium 7.5 mg/dL,and albumin 2 g/dL. Which one of the following is the most appropriate change for this patient's discharge prescriptions?
options: B. Increase dose of lorazepam to 2 mg.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Even with resolving mucositis, most patients will have some element of diarrhea when recovering from high-dose chemotherapy. Additionally, this patient has hypokalemia with a potassium concentration of 2.9mEq/L. The patient will most likely continue to have electrolyte imbalances requiring replacement for a few weeks and should be continually assessed at follow-up appointments (Answer A is correct). With engraftment comes the resolution of mucositis and usually nausea/vomiting, so it is expected that the patient will need less antiemetics or narcotics at discharge (Answer B and Answer C are ncomect). Calcium supplementation is an option, but the corrected calcium is within an aceptable range whereas the potassium is more critical (Answer C is incorrect).

questions.question: A 67-year-old man is undergoing treatment with cyclophosphamide and busulfan for chronic myeloid leukemia. He has a history of extensive nausea and is receiving lorazepam and promethazine four times/ day. He is receiving methotrexate plus cyclosporine as GVHD prophylaxis. On day 1, his sodium is decreased to 122 mEq/L.Which one of the following drugs is most likely responsible for the change in this patient's sodium?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Preparative regimen dosage during an allogeneic HCT may produce adverse events more ofen than with conventional dosage chemotherapy. This patient is experiencing the lyndrome of inappropriate diuretic hormone secondary to cyclophosphamide Mdministration, which commonly presents as asymptomatic hyponatremia that resolves Within a few days (Answer C is correct). Electrolyte abnormalities from cyclosporine fan occur, but they usually affect potassium and magnesium, not sodium (Answer A is Mcorrect). Methotrexate as a cause is inappropriate because the patient is on day -I and will not receive the drug until day +1 (Answer B is incorrect). Promethazine may result M the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone; however, given the timing of Cyclophosphamide and history of promethazine use, promethazine is incorrect (Answef Dis incorreet).

questions.question: A 59-year-old man is about to receive his first dose of cyclophosphamide and thiotepa for acute myeloid leukemia followed by an allogeneic transplantation. He has a history of a myocardial infarction, diabetes, and blood clots. Which one of the following monitoring parameters is most relevant before cyclophosphamide administration?
options: A. Urine red blood cell count.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Ihe nonmyelo-suppressive dose-limiting toxicity of cyclophosphamide is cardiotoxiciry Because this patient has a medical history of coronary artery diseese, preemptive monitoring with electrocardiography is pertinent (Answer B is correct). Hematuria plasma sodium, and urine sodium play a role in the monitoring of acute toxicities associated with cyclophosphamide, but they are not appropriate for pretreatment monitoring (Answer A, Answer C, and Answer D are incorrect).

questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning the musculoskeletal abnormalities in patients with sickle cell disease is correct?
options: A. Hand-foot syndrome characterized by diffuse swelling, tenderness, and warmth of the hands and feet in children under the age of 5 leads to chronic disability in about 10% of patients.
B. Acute arthritis seen in patients with sickle cell crisis is often associated with high white cell counts in joint effusions.
C. The bone pain in sickle cell crisis is due to bone and bone marrow infarction.
D. Acute gouty arthritis is common in patients with sickle cell disease.
E. Total hip replacement is contraindicated in patients with sickle cell anemia who sustain avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Several musculoskeletal abnormalities are associated with sickle cell disease. Children may develop diffuse swelling, tenderness, and warmth of the hands and feet, termed sickle cell dactylitis or hand-foot syndrome, which is self.limited and not associated with long-term damage. Blood cell formation in the distal extremities decreases with age; this syndrome is rarely seen after age 5. Although sickle cell crisis is often associated with arthritis of the knees and elbows, joint effusions tend to be noninflammatory with low white cell counts and a predominance of mononuclear cells. Osteomyelitis is common, particularly with salmonella, and occasionally septic arthritis can occur. The major problems during sickle cell crisis is sickled red cellmediated bone infarction, which is quite painful. Radiographic manifestations of such infarction include periosteal elevation and irregular thickening of the bone cortex. In its most extreme form this bony infarction can produce avascular necrosis of the head of the femur, which occurs in about 5% of patients. If this process is severe, total hip replacement may be quite beneficial. Although patients with sickle cell disease are often hyperuricemic, gouty arthritis is uncommon. Bone marrow hyperplasia with associated widening of the medullary cavities and thinning of the cortex can result in cupping of the vertebral bodies (fish-bone deformity on radiographs) and vertebral compression.

questions.question: A 70-year-old man of Irish descent returns to his physician for a routine check of his blood pressure. He is a vigorous, retired executive who except for mild hypertension is healthy. After his examination, as he is getting dressed, he states that his wife has been nagging him to mention a spot on his nose (as shown in Plate P). He is certain that this lesion, which has been present for several years, is of no significance. The most likely diagnosis for this lesion is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is E. Basal cell carcinoma is the most common malignancy in the United States. The typical appearance is that of a slowly enlarging, pearly translucent papule with rolled borders and overlying telangiectasias. As the lesion enlarges, central ulceration may occur(rodent ulcer). Sun-exposed areas are most commonly involved-about 90% of tumors occur on the head and neck-and fair-skinned persons are at greatest risk. Dermal nevi,which occur commonly on the faces of adults, lack the translucency seen in basal cell carcinoma. Sebaceous hyperplasia is usually smaller and has a distinct yellowish color.Diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma is easily established by punch or incisional biopsy.

questions.question: A 52-year-old woman sees her physician for an "insurancephysical." Physical examination reveals only a pigmented lesion (as shown in Plate Q) present on one foot.The woman states that the lesion apparently was present at birth and does not itch or bleed; it is, however, not as homogeneous in color as it used to be. Which of the following statements about the condition described is true?
options: A. Bleeding and tenderness would be the first signs of malignant degeneration.
B. It is unlikely that the lesion, present since birth, is malignant.
C. The diagnostic procedure of choice is an incisional biopsy of this lesion.
D. Change in color of the lesion is a suspicious sign for potential malignancy.
E. Early diagnosis of this lesion would not affect prognosis.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The characteristics that distinguish superficial spreading malignant melanoma from a normal mole include irregularity of its border and variegation of color. Instead of the homogeneous color and regular borders of a "normal" mole, the lesion shows disorderliness and irregularity. The first changes noted by persons who develop melanoma in a preexisting mole are a "darkening" in color or a change in the borders of the lesion. Irregularity of the borders in an expanding, darkening mole is melanoma until proved otherwise; excisional (not incisional) biopsy should be done promptly because early diagnosis and excision reduce the mortality. it is best not to cut into a lesion for which melanoma is in the differential diagnosis.

questions.question: A 58-year-old man presents with fatigue. His physical examination is normal except for the presence of splenomegaly. CBC discloses hematocrit, 29%; platelet count,90,000/ L; WBC, 2700/ L; and an essentially normal red cell morphology (differential 12% monocytes, 12% granulocytes, and 76% lymphocytes). A bone marrow aspirate and biopsy were performed. The aspirate was dry and the biopsy is pending. Based on the available information, the most likely diagnosis in this case is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Pancytopenia with a dry marrow aspirate argues against CLL and myeloma. Normal RBC morphology argues against myelofibrosis. The WBC count and differential count argue against CML. Hairy cell leukemia is a neoplasm of mature B lymphocytes typically presenting with pancytopenia, splenomegaly, and a dry bone marrow aspirate.Patients with hairy cell leukemia are prone to infections with unusual microorganisms,such as atypical mycobacteria; they tend to be granulocytopenic and have a preponderance of mature-appearing lymphocytes in the peripheral blood that have, on close inspection or on ultrastructural analysis, multiple hairlike projections. Bone marrow biopsies typically yield a "fried egg" appearance in that the cells appear to be separated from one another, due to these projections and fixation artifacts generated from them. Immunophenotypically, hairy cells are characterized by the presence of mature B cell markers as well as the CD25 antigen, which is the low affinity IL-2 receptor. Fortunately, there are many treatment modalities available for patients with hairy cell leukemia. The current treatment of choice is a 7-day intravenous infusion of 2-chlorodeoxyadenosine. This single course of treatment results in complete remissions in 80% of patients. Other effective modalities include splenectomy, interferon，or pentostatin (deoxycoformycin).

questions.question: A 58-year-old chronic alcoholic and heavy smoker presents with a 3-cm, firm, right mid cervical neck mass. An excisional biopsy reveals squamous cell carcinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach at this time?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Patients who are heavy smokers and drinkers are at increased risk to develop squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. In fact, the risk for those who both smoke and drink is muliplicatively increased compared with those who abuse just one of these substances. A firm neck mass in a patient with these habits should prompt an aggressive search for a primary lesion in the head and neck region and would include panendoscopy Caryngoscopy, esophagoscopy, and bronchoscopy) with biopsy of all suspicious areas.Squamous cell carcinoma in the midcervical chain in the presence of a normal physical examination (thereby excluding large tumors of the mouth or supraglottic region) could represent a metastasis from an infraglottic primary. Therefore, the best way to ascertain the diagnosis in this case is to perform a careful upper aerodigestive examination, which should begin with indirect laryngoscopy. CT of the neck, while helpful in delineating the extent of disease, would likely not reveal the primary. Treatment planning optimally requires delineation of the primary and definition of lymph node metastases. The standard approach to a primary head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with a large lymph node metastasis is radiation therapy or surgery or both. However, use of induction chemotherapy is being investigated as a possible means both to improve survival and to reduce the amount of disfiguring local therapy that would be required in such instances.

questions.question: A 28-year-old man with newly diagnosed acute myelogenous leukemia spikes a temperature to 38.7 C (101.7 F) on the sixth day of induction therapy. He feels well and has no physical complaints. His only medicine is intravenous cytosine arabinoside, 140 mg every 12 h. Physical examination is unrevealing. His white blood count is 900/ L, of which 10% are granulocytes and the rest mostly lymphocytes; platelet count is 24,000/L. Findings on chest x-ray and urinalysis are normal. After obtaining appropriate cultures, the man's physician should
options: A. observe closely for the development of a clinically evident source of fever
B. begin antibiotic therapy with gentamicin and mezlocillin
C. begin granulocyte transfusion and antibiotic therapy with gentamicin and mezlocillin
D. begin gammaglobulin treatment and antibiotic therapy with gentamicin and mezlocillin
E. begin antibiotic therapy with amphotericin, gentamicin, and mezlocillin
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Attacked promptly, infection in neutropenic patients can be quickly fatal. Often, these patients display neither the signs nor the symptoms of infection. Fever should be Tegarded as an indication of infection, and antibiotic therapy should begin immediately afier appropriate cultures are obtained. An effective initial antibiotic regimen would Consist of an aminoglycoside antibiotic or third-generation cephalosporin and a Semisynthetic antipseudomonal penicillin. Gammaglobulin is of little benefit in the lreatment of granulocytopenic cancer patients. Granulocyte transfusions are of no benefit. Amphotericin B is appropriate if granulocytopenia persists and defervescence does not occur after 7 days of antibacterial antibiotics, or sooner, if clinical deterioration is noted.

questions.question: Coumarin-induced skin necrosis is occasionally associated with the institution of oral anticoagulants in patients with
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Several reports have described the association of coumarin- induced skin necrosis in patients with congenital protein C deficiency. The skin lesions occur on the breasts,buttocks, legs, and penis. They appear to be a result of diffuse thrombosis of the venules with interstitial bleeding. This condition is presumed to result from an imbalance in hemostatic mechanism activity favoring thrombosis during the early phases of coumarin administration. Protein C has a relatively short half-life within the circulation (about 14 h) compared with that of some of the vitamin K- dependent procoagulant clotting factors (factor X and prothrombin), and a rapid drop in its effective concentration could produce such a situation. However, only about one-third of cases of coumarin- induced skin necrosis are related to protein C deficiency.

questions.question: A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department because her family notes that she has yellow skin. The patient has lost 7 kg (15 Ibs) over the past 3 months but states that this is because she has been dieting in preparation for her daughter's wedding. Her past medical history is significant only for vitiligo. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for the presence of scleral icterus and a yellow tinge to the skin. Laboratory evaluation reveals hematocrit of 17%, WBC count of 2500/ L,and platelet count of 70,000/ L. Serum chemistries are normal except for direct bilirubir of 51 mol/ L (3 mg/dL) and indirect bilirubin of 12 mol/L (0.7 mg/ dL). The patient's reticulocyte count is 3%. MCV is 108 fL. Which one of the following additional laboratory findings would most likely be associated with this patient's clinical syndrome?
options: A. Clonal chromosomal abnormalities on karyotypic analysis of the bone marrow
questions.explanation: The correct answer is E. While pancytopenia is frequently due to an intrinsic bone marrow abnormality, vitamin B and i2 folate deficiency may also present with low blood counts. The elevated red cell volume coupled with a low reticulocyte index suggests a megaloblastic anemia. The history of vitiligo represents one of the several autoimmune-type diseases associated with pernicious anemia (PA). Other such immunologically mediated diseases include Graves' disease, myxedema, thyroiditis, idiopathic adrenocortical insufficiency, and hypoparathyroidism. PA is a failure of gastric production of intrinsic factor due to autoimmune destruction of parietal cells, which prevents B absorption in the distal ileum. Antibody-mediated de- 12 struction of parietal cells results in achlorhydria (an abnormally high gastric pH). The hematologic abnormalities of PA include elevated MCV, decreased reticulocyte count, hypersegmented neutrophil nuclei, and megaloblastic changes in the bone marrow that can, if severe, be confused with acute leukemia. Extramedullary manifestations of PA include neurologic abnormalities typified by demyelinization of the posterior and lateral spinal columns of the spinal cord, resulting in numbness and parasthesia, weakness, and ataxia. Patients with megaloblastic anemia on the basis of deficiency of intrinsic factor respond to cyanocobalamin injections within several days. Hypokalemia may complicate the recovery phase.

questions.question: A 43-year-old woman was diagnosed as having an infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the right breast when she was 41. The lesion was 3 cm in diameter. Lymph node examination was negative. Estrogen and progesterone receptors were negative. She underwent a lumpectomy, followed by radiation therapy to the breast and chest wall,followed by six cycles of cyclophosphamide plus doxorubicin chemotherapy. At this time she feels weli but has two 2-cm nodules in each lung on chest radiography. These were not present on prior chest radiographs. In discussing the situation with the patient,which of the following statements is correct?
options: A. These nodules are a late manifestation of cyclophosphamide toxicity.
B. Tamoxifen therapy should be employed at this time.
C. Autologous bone marrow transplantation offers this patient the best chance for long-term disease free survival.
D. An antibody to the erbB2 proto-oncogene may improve the response to chemotherapy.
E. The patient has a median survival of approximately 6 to 12 months.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Despite having a negative lymph node exam at the time Of her original diagnosis 2 years earlier, this patient is at relatively high risk for recurrence because of the size of her tumor. Shereceived appropriate adjuvant chemotherapy given this risk;unfortunately, this treatment did not eliminate the eventual clinical relapse manifested by the two lung nodules. In this patient the prior probability of these lung nodules being due to her original breast cancer is very high. Whether or not to do a needle biopsy of lesions to confimn the presence of breast cancer would be somewhat controversial. If the patient were a nonsmoker, the chances of the lesions being anything other than breast cancer is very low. Patients with metastatic breast cancer may live with the disease for several years but are not known to benefit from a myelointensive approach. Once a patient has metastatic breast cancer, bisphosphonate therapy may be of benefit in reducing the risk of skeletal complications. In those ( 20%) of patients whose tumors overexpress the erbB2 proto-oncogene, the addition of an antibody to this molecule (herceptin) can improve the results when compared to the use of pacitaxel chemotherapy alone.

questions.question: A 27-year-old woman presents with stage II (breast and lymph node involvement)light breast cancer. Her family history is markedly positive for other tumors. One of her sisters developed an estrogenic sarcoma at age 17, her brother was diagnosed with acute leukemia at age 5, her mother died of breast cancer, and she has two uncles with softtissue sarcomas, both developing this disease when in their thirties. This patient's peripheral blood lymphocytes would be most likely to reveal which of the following abnormalities?
options: E. Mutations of epidermal growth factor receptor gene
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The most common genetic alteration in human cancer is mutation or deletion of the p53 gene, which is found on the long arm of chromosome 17. Wild type p53 suppresses malignant transformation of cells in tissue culture. It appears to regulate cell cycle progression by holding cells at the G checkpoint. Like the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor gene, p53 may be I activated by protein products of transforming viruses. A rare autosomal dominant cancer syndrome, the Li-Fraumeni syndrome, is characterized by families with a very high incidence of a diverse spectrum of childhood and adult tumors, including breast cancer, soft tissue sarcomas, brain tumors, bone sarcomas,Jeukemia, and adrenocortical carcinoma. Germ line mutations in the p53 gene have been found in several of these families. Since an abnormality of one allele of p53 is inherited,these patients are at risk of developing homozygous p53 loss and a predisposition to neoplastic transformation. Mutations of the p53 gene are also very common in sporadic human tumors.

questions.question: A patient with a myelodysplastic syndrome (subtype, refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts) has been transfusion-dependent for the past 2 years. The patient has received a total of 50 units of packed red blood cells. His physical examination is normal except for hyperpigmentation. Laboratory evaluation reveals mild glucose intolerance. A trial of erythropoietin was unsuccessful. Which of the following would be the most important therapeutic approach at this time?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Since each unit of transfused blood contains 200 to 250 mg of iron and normal iron excretion is only 1 mg/d, a patient receiving about 40 units of blood annually will accumulate about 8 g of iron, putting him or her at risk for problems related to transfusional iron overload. In addition to the requirement for many transfusions, the disorder must also have a long natural history to allow for the development of the clinical sequelae of chronic iron overload. Thalassemia major, myeloproliferative disorders, myelodysplastic syndromes (without excess myeloblasts), pure red cell aplasia, and moderately severe aplastic anemia are diseases that may be associated with transfusional iron overload. The spectrum of problems produced by iron deposition in tissues includes cardiac dysfunction (arrhythmias, conduction defects, and restrictive cardiomyopathy), hepatic cirrhosis, glucose intolerance, gonadal dysfunction, and hyperpigmentation due to increased melanin production secondary to dermal iron deposition. The only available treatment for transfusion-associated hemochromatosis(phlebotomy is not an option because of chronic anemia) is chelation with desferrioxamine, which must be given subcutaneously over 12 to 16 h/d by a portable pump. While oral ascorbic acid may enhance iron excretion in patients receiving desferrioxamine, it has no role as a monotherapy and may be associatedwith dangerous cardiac toxicity.

questions.question: A 26-year-old woman has painful mouth ulcers. Six weeks ago, she was started on propylthiouracil for hyperthyroidism. She is afebrile, and physical examination is unremarkable except for several small oral aphthous ulcers. White blood cell count is 200/L (15% neutrophils, 80% lymphocytes, 5% monocytes); hemoglobin concentration,hematocrit, and platelet count are normal. The woman's physician should stop the prophylthiouracil and
options: A. schedule a follow-up outpatient appointment
B. arrange for HLA typing of her siblings in preparation for bone marrow transplantation
D. hospitalize her for broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy
E. hospitalize her for white blood cell transfusion
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Severe neutropenia is a rare idiosyncratic reaction to certain drugs, including Propylthiouracil. In addition to having sore throat and oral and anal mucosal ulcerations,affected persons are susceptible to overwhelming, life threatening infections. However,in the absence of fever or clinical signs of infection, they should be followed as Outpatients, saving them exposures to nosocomial pathogens in the hospital. Empirical use of broad-spectrum antibiotics without fever or other signs of infection is not advisable, and glucocorticoid therapy is not useful. White blood cell transfusion can be accompanied by serious morbidity (i.e.,pulmonary leukostasis). Because severe drug induced neutropenia is generally self-limited once use of the offending drug has been Vlopped, consideration of bone marrow transplantation is not justified.

questions.question: An 18-year-old black man undergoing a physical examination prior to playing college sports is found to have a normal CBC except that the MCV is 72 fL. Subsequent testing reveals a normal metabisulfite test and a normal hemoglobin electrophoresis.Which of the following conditions most likely accounts for these findings?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is E. Hemoglobinopathies are a diverse group of congenital disorders characterized by one or more mutations in one of the genes coding for hemoglobin chains. The clinical consequences can range from no effect to incompatibility with life. Microcytosis occurs in these conditions except for the silent thalassemia carrier state in which only one of the four globin genes is deleted. Such persons have no hematologic abnormalities.Persons with deletion of two of the four chain genes (thalassemia trait) tend to have microcytic and slightly hypochromic red cells without significant hemolysis or anemia.Hemoglobin electrophoresis may be normal or may reveal a decreased amount of hemoglobin A2. Deletion of three of the four chain genes, so-called hemoglobin H disease, is associated with significant anemia and with a production of hemoglobin H(chain tetramers) on hemoglobin electrophoresis. There are only two genes coding for the globin chain. Patients with abnormalities in one such chain have thalassemia trait characterized by microcytosis, abnormal-appearing red cells, and an elevated level of hemoglobin A2 or F or both on hemoglobin electrophoresis. Any patient who inherits at least one allele with a hemoglobin S mutation (sickle hemoglobin, valine to glutamic acid substitution at the sixth amino acid of the globin chain) will demonstrate red blood cell sickling under reduced oxygen tension, as is artificially produced by addition of an oxygen-consuming agent such as metabisulfite to the blood. Therefore, any patient with sickle cell trait, sickle cell anemia, or a compound heterozygote such as sickle thalassemia or sickle C will have a positive metabisulfite test (and would also have a positive hemoglobin electrophoresis). Hemoglobin E is a very common hemoglobin variant that is highly prevalent in Southeast Asia. Patients with this disorder have an abnormal hemoglobin electrophoresis, slightly macrocytic red cells, and target cells, but no anemia or other clinical manifestations unless they also inherit thalassemia.

questions.question: A 30-year-old black woman with long-standing sickle cell anemia presents with severe pain in the chest and abdomen I week after having an upper respiratory infection. No intrathoracic or intra-abdominal pathology was immediately obvious on toutine physical examination and laboratory evaluation. The most appropriate therapeutic intervention at this point is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. clinical problems arising in patients with sickle cell anemia are due to vasoocclusive phenomena caused by sickling of deoxygenated red blood cells in capillaries.Microinfarcts can occur suddenly and cause severe pain in almost any part of the body,although the abdomen, chest, back, and joints are most commonly affected. These crises may be precipitated by upper respiratory infection, cold weather, or dehydration,Unfortunately, it is often difficult to distinguish between a painful sickle abdominal crisis and an actual acute abdominal emergency. Pleuritic chest pain and fever may occur in the absence of an infiltrate. If an infiltrate does occur, distinguishing between pneumonia and pulmonary infarction is difficult, although culture and Gram stain of the sputum might be helpful in this regard. In addition to painful crises, microinfarcts can cause chronic damage in the lungs, kidneys, liver, skeleton, and skin. Painful crises should mandate the use of adequate analgesia, including narcotics, and hydration.Unfortunately, there is an increased risk of opiate addiction in this patient population.Oxygen is helpful if hypoxemia complicates a painful crisis. The role of transfusional therapy in sickle cell anemia is controversial. There is some evidence to suggest that use of aggressive transfusions may decrease the frequency of painful crises, but such an approach has little role in an ongoing crisis. Hydroxyurea therapy may reduce the incidence of sickle crises by increasing synthesis of fetal hemoglobin. Antibiotics should be administered only in the setting of documented infection.

questions.question: In persons who have chronic myelogenous leukemia, the translocation that accounts for the Philadelphia chromosome most commonly is found in
options: A. all cells of the body
B. all three hematopoietic cell lines but not in nonhematopoietic cells
C. all cells of the granulocytic cell line but not in nongranulocytic cells
D. all bone marrow stem cells but not in mature cells
E. all bone marrow stem cells and certain mature granulocytes
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. In about 95% of persons who have CML, material comprising approximately one-half of the long arm of chromosome 22 is translocated to the end of chromosome 9. This abnormality, called the Philadelphia chromosome, can be found in all hematopoietic cell Jines. It is thought to represent an acquired somatic cell mutation in the bone marrow,with preferential survival and proliferation of the affected cell clone. The pathogenesis of chronic myelogenous leukemia is therefore a paradigm for all cancers that are believed to arise from a single cell that gives rise to the malignant clone. Normal stem cells exist in the marrow of patients with CML, but they are suppressed by the malignant cells.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes the relationship between testicular tumors and serum markers?
options: A. Pure seminomas produce alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) or human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in 90% of cases.
B. More than 40% of non seminomatous germ cell tumors produce no cell markers
C. Both hCG and AFP should be measured in following the progress of a tumor.
D. Measurement of tumor markers the day following surgery for localized disease is useful in determining completeness of the resection.
E. hCG is limited in its usefulness as a marker, because it is identical to human luteinizing hormone.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Ninety percent of persons with nonseminomatous germ cell tumors produce either AFP or B-hCG; in contrast, persons with pure seminomas usually produce neither. These tumor markers are present for some time after surgery if the presurgical levels are high,30 days or more may be required before meaningful postsurgical levels can be obtained.The half-lives of AFP and B-hCG are 6 days and I day, respectively. After treatment,unequal reduction of B-hCG and AFP may occur, suggesting that the two markers are synthesized by heterogeneous clones of cells within the tumor; thus, both markers should be followed. B-hCG is similar to luteinizing hormone except for its distinctive beta subunit.

questions.question: A 45-year-old man presents with fatigue. Two years ago the patient received six cycles of combination chemotherapy (each cycle consisted of cyclophosphamide,doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone) for non-Hodgkin's lymphoma in chest and abdominal sites. The patient entered complete remission and has been followed expectantly since that point. His last prior visit was 3 months ago at which time he had no evidence of recurrent lymphoma, felt well, and had a normal laboratory examination.At this time his physical examination is remarkable for a purple discoloration of the fingertips, ears, and nose. The patient is somewhat pale. There is no evidence for peripheral lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies include the following: white count 10,000/_L (differential 60% neutrophils, 10% bands, 10% lymphocytes, 10%monocytes, 3% eosinophils, 1% basophils, 2% metamyelocytes, 1% myelocytes, and 1%nucleated red blood cell), hematocrit 28% and platelet count 300,000/ L. The following results are also found: MCV 98 fL, lactic dehydrogenase 6.8 kat/L (400 U/L), total bilirubin 51 mol/L (3.0 mg/dL), and direct bilirubin 5.1 mol/L (0.3 mg/dL). Review of the peripheral blood smear reveals clumped red cells. A routine direct Coombs' test is negative. Additional laboratory testing would most likely reveal
options: A. positive direct Coombs' test (using anti-IgG antisera) if specimen is processed without allowing cooling
B. positive indirect Coombs' test detected with anti- IgG antibodies
C. circulating antibodies against Epstein-Barr virus
D. circulating antibodies against fetal red blood cells
E. circulating antibodies against Mycoplasma pneumoniae
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. If patients develop circulating anti-lgM antibodies with specificity for polysaccharide antigens on red cell membranes, they may suffer from so called cold-reactive hemolysis.The clinical manifestations of the presence of such antibodies are hemolysis, which is generally not severe, and a mild elevation of the reticulocyte count, agglutination of red cells, and an increased rate of hemolysis at temperatures 37 C (98.6 F). A second clinical manifestation of cold hemolysis is the presence of acrocyanosis, characterized by marked purple discoloration of the extremities, ears, and nose during cooling. IgM antibodies may be missed if the blood is allowed to cool after it is drawn because of adsorption onto the patient's own red blood cells and subsequent removal as the blood clots. Therefore, the blood should be allowed to clot at a warm temperature. Serologic analysis will reveal a positive direct Coombs' test if anti-C3 antisera is used. The activation of complement by the fixed IgM molecules results in the marked accumulation of the C3dg degradation product on the red cell surface, allowing detection in this fashion. The specificity of the cold agglutinin antibody may be helpful in that a leaction with adult red cells compared with fetal (cord) blood is more common in benign lymphoproliferative disorders. On the other hand, antibodies that react more strongly with fetal cells compared with adult cells are called anti-i and are generally seen in lymphomas and in infectious mononucleosis. The patient in this question may well have A recurrence of his lymphoma, which is presenting as a cold hemolytic disease because Of the presence of monoclonal IgM antibody. This problem is best treated by successful anti-lymphoma therapy.

questions.question: A 70-year-old man presents with back pain and fatigue. Workup reveals hematocrit of 30%, white blood cell count of 3.5/mL, and platelet count of 220,000/mL. Serum calcium and serum creatinine are normal. However, serum protein electrophoresis reveals a monoclonal protein of 42 g/L (4.2 g/dL), proved to be IgG-κ based on immunoelectrophoresis. Bone marrow examination dis38 closes sheets of dysplastic plasme cells, and skeletal survey reveals multiple osteolytic legions in the skull and spine. The patient is started on melphalan, prednisone, and erythropoietin. Which of the following would be most reasonable to add to the patient's therapeutic regimen at this time?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. This patient has classic symptomatic multiple myeloma. Although not in renal failure and not hypercalcemic, the patient has several markers of high tumor burden, including heavy plasma cell infiltration of the bone marrow and multiple osteolytic lesions in the bony skeleton. Initial chemotherapy could reasonably include either high-dose dexamethasone; combination chemotherapy with vincristine, doxorubicin, and dexamethasone; or a combination of the alkylating agent melphalan and prednisone Erythropoietin is given because this drug has a reasonable chance to ameliorate the anemia associated with this disease. Bisphosphonates have been shown to reduce the bony destruction caused by the myeloma cells by interference with osteoclastic activity,thereby reducing liberation of bony calcium. Perhaps because of their ability to stabilize the bony matrix, bisphosphonates have been shown in randomized controlled trials to reduce lytic disease compared to placebo. In a randomized study performed by the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group, the rate of skeletal events was twice as high in the placebo group compared with the pamidronate treated group. There was also a survival benefit associated with pamidronate use (in those who had received more than one antimyeloma treatment). Oral pamidronate has not been as successful in reducing complications of myeloma as was the intravenous preparation. Bisphosphonates may have a primary anti-myeloma effect, perhaps by induction of apoptosis (programmed cell death) in myeloma cell lines. As such, the current standard of care is to administer intravenous bisphosphonates at the beginning of chemotherapy and to continue treatment indefinitely.

questions.question: A 25-year-old, previously healthy woman presents with jaundice, confusion, and fever. Initial physical examination is unremarkable except for scattered petechiae on the lower extremities, scleral icterus, and disorientation on mental status examination.Laboratory examination discloses the following: hematocrit, 27%; white cell count,12,000/ L; platelet count, 10,000/_L; bilirubin, 85 mol/ L (5 mg/dL); direct bilirubin, 10 mol/L (0.6 mg/ dL)j; urea nitrogen, 21 mmol/L (60 mg/dL); creatinine, 400 mol/L (4.5 mg/dL.). Red blood cell smear discloses fragmented red blood cells and nucleated red blood cells. Prothrombin, thrombin, and partial thromboplastin times are all normal. The most effective and appropriate therapeutic maneuver is likely to be
options: D. administration of high-dose glucocorticoids plus cyclophosphamide
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. This young woman is suffering from a combination of hemolytic anemia with fragmented red cells in the absence of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC),thrombocytopenia, fever, mental status changes, and renal dysfunction, which is essentially pathognomonic of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). The pathogenesis is believed to be due to an antibody against a protease that normally cleaves von Will brand's factor. Pathologically, arteriolar hyalinization, which is also seen in DIC, may be noted. Seventy percent of patients with TTP improve with exchange transfusion or plasmapheresis. Glucocorticoids, antiplatelet agents,splenectomy, and vincristine have been of benefit to subsets of patients, but each is less effective and probably associated with a greater risk than therapeutic plasmapheresis.

questions.question: A 38-year-old woman presents with redness and burning in the distal extremities.She has no other complaints. She has never been pregnant. Physical examination is normal except for redness of the fingertips and splenomegaly. Laboratory examination reveals hematocrit 40%, WBC count 9000 with a normal differential, and platelet count of 950,000/ L. Other laboratory studies include reticulocyte count of 1%, bone marrow examination that discloses a hypercellular marrow with megakaryocytic hyperplasia and hyperlobated megakaryocytes, absent collagen deposition, and the presence of normal amounts of bone marrow iron. Cytogenetic studies reveal a normal female karyotype. A red cell mass study is normal. Which of the following statements concerning the patient's condition is true?
options: C. Oral administration of chlorambucil, 0.4 mg/kg daily for 5 days, should begin.
D. Aspirin, 2 tablets every 6 h, should be administered.
E. Hydroxyurea, 1000 mg daily orally, is indicated.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is E. When a patient presents with thrombocytosis, it is important to determine if this abnormality is due to a myeloproliferative disorder or is reactive due to infection,malignancy, hemolytic anemia, the postoperative state, hemorrhage, iron deficiency,drug reaction, chronic inflammatory disease, response to exercise, recovery from myelosuppression, recovery from B deficiency, or even myelodysplastic syndrome(either 5q-syndrome or rare cases of sideroblastic anemia). Once secondary causes of thrombocytosis have been satisfactorily excluded, then it is important to delineate the specific myeloproliferative disorder. The normal red cell mass virtually excludes polycythemia vera, and normal cytogenetics makes the diagnosis of chronic myelogenous leukemia most unlikely. Anemia, massive splenomegaly, teardrop red cell forms, or an elevated white count would advance consideration of agnogenic myeloid metaplasia/ myelofibrosis. However, the bone marrow examination did not disclose excess collagen fibrosis. As such, the patient in this question has essential thrombocythemia. Patients with this disease may develop hemorrhage or thrombotic pomplications. Older patients have a higher risk of thrombosis; some younger patients can be observed. However, this patient is symptomatic due to erythromelalgia, the syndrome of redness and painful burning of the distal extremities caused by localized platelet aggregation. Chronic use of alkylating agents should be avoided due to the risk of leukemogenesis. Antiplatelet agents may protect against thrombosis but could lead to severe hemorrhage. Splenectomy would result in an even higher platelet count. The best treatment in this patient is probably the use of hydroxyurea at a dose titrated to lower the platelet count to below 500,000. Interferon may be a useful alternative for those patients uable to tolerate hydroxyurea. Anagrelide is also effective at lowering platelet counts,but it must be given continuously to maintain its effects.

questions.question: 201. A 42-year-old woman presents with epistaxis and gum bleeding. Physical examination is remarkable for a temperature of 38 C (100.4 F) and petechiae on the lower extremities. Laboratory evaluation includes a hematocrit of 29%, platelet count of 5,000/ L, and WBC of 2100/ L (differential including 22% blasts, 30% promyelocytes, 20% lymphocytes, 10% monocytes, 2% myelocytes, and 3% metamyelocytes). PT is 15 s and PTT is 55 s. Bone marrow examination discloses a hypercellular marrow infiltrated with myeloblasts and heavily granulated promyelocytes. Myeloperoxidase stain of a bone marrow aspirate smear is markedly positive and demonstrates numerous intracellular rod like forms. The patient is begun on all-trans retinoic acid. Which of the following is the most likely complication of this therapy?
options: A. Worsening of disseminated intravascular coagulopathy
questions.explanation: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APML) [M3 according to the FAB (French-American-British) classification system] is characterized by bone marrow infiltration with malignant-appearing promyelocytes. Distinctive features of this entity compared with other subtypes of de novo acute myeloid leukemia include the common presentation with leukopenia, the frequent development of DIC due to release of procoagulant granules from the promyelocytes, and the pathognomonic demonstration of a translocation between chromosomes 15 and 17 on cytogenetic analysis. This translocation juxtaposes sequences from the retinoic acid-receptor alpha gene on chromosome 17 with another DNA binding protein, called PML, on chromosome 17. The resultant fusion protein plays some role in preventing normal differentiation. Interestingly, even before the documentation of the genetic basis for this translocation, it was noted by investigators in China that the use of all-trans retinoic acid, an orally administered vitamin A derivative, led to complete remissions in the vast majority of patients with APML. The mechanism of action of this drug appears to be induction of differentiation of the malignant clone. As such, patients enter remission slowly over a period of 30 to 60 days. DIC, typically made worse by chemotherapy, is rapidly ameliorated by all-trans retinoic acid. Other cytotoxic effects of chemotherapy, such as mucositis and myelosuppression, do not occur with all-trans retinoic acid. Common side effects include dry skin and peeling at the corners of the mouth. A life-threatening complication, occurring in 20% of patients treated with all-trans retinoic acid, is the so-called retinoic acid syndrome, manifested by pulmonary infiltrates and incipient respiratory failure, sometimes associated with a high white count. Glucocorticoids, leukopheresis, and hydroxyurea have each been associated with some improvement. Patients given all-trans retinoic acid alone will eventually relapse, so initial induction therapy with all-trans retinoic acid should be combined with chemotherapy.

questions.question: 202. Which of the following statements regarding toxic effects of chemotherapy is correct?
