Cold agglutinins are circulating IgM antibodies that may increase in response to certain infections such as Mycoplasma pneumonia, and can induce cold agglutinins mediated autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Plasmapheresis is very efficient in removing big circulating molecules such as the pentameric IgM rather than the relatively small dimeric IgG molecules. IgG type antibodies are responsible for SLE associated hemolytic anemia.

questions.question:
295. A 35-year-old man of Northern European origin underwent a routine medical examination and was found to have a 10-cm splenomegaly. He works as an administrator and has never travelled outside Europe. He is otherwise well and has no other physical findings. A blood test shows: Hb is 12.3 g/dl; WCC 62 × 109/l; platelets 542 ×109/.
What is the most likely cause of his splenomegaly?
questions.explanation: Chronic myeloid leukemia .Splenomegaly can be classified as: Hematological malignant, Chronic myeloid leukemia, chronic lymphocytic leukemia, acute leukemia,lymphoma, myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera, Hemolysis Sickle-cell disease,autoimmune hemolytic anemia, megaloblastic anemia, Portal hypertension Cirrhosis,portal vein thrombosis Storage diseases Gaucher's disease, Niemann-Pick disease,histiocytosis X Systemic diseases Sarcoidosis, amyloidosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis ,Acute infections Bacterial endocarditis, typhoid,infectious mononucleosis Chronic infections Tuberculosis, brucellosis, syphilis, malaria,leishmaniasis, schistosomiasis

questions.question: 296.A 10-year-old boy is referred for investigation of anemia. He is generally well but is small for his age. He is progressing well for his age group at school. A male first cousin died of leukaemia. On examination the child is pale and has a few bruises. He is noted to have markedly thickened nails and is below the third centile in height. A blood count shows: Hb is 7.2 g/dl; WCC 1.2 x 109/L; platelets 20 x 109/L. What is the most likely explanation for his anaemia?
questions.explanation: Dyskeratosis congenital. Congenital aplastic anaemias include Fanconi's anemia and dyskeratosis congenita. Dyskeratosis congenita is characterized by skin pigmentation,nail dystrophy, leucoplakia and a predisposition to bone marrow failure and malignancy.It has been reported as X-linked recessive, autosomal-dominant and autosomal-recessive diseases. The X-linked recessive form was linked to chromosome Xq28 and the gene DKCI, which encodes for a ubiquitously expressed protein dyskerin. The age of presentation with pancytopenia is variable, with a median age of 8 years. Patients may progress to acute leukemia. Patients who are progressing to pancytopenia may be cured by bone marrow transplantation.

questions.question: 297. A 74-year-old woman presented with a 2-day history of extensive bruising. She had a history of ischemic heart disease and was a heavy smoker. Her regular medication was amlodipine and aspirin. She had recently started quinine sulphate for night cramps. Her Hb is i1.4 g/dl, MCV 87 fl, MCH 30 pg, MCHC 31 g/dl, WCC 7.2 x 109/L with a normal differential and platelets 11 x 109/L. Urea and electrolytes are normal. What is the most likely cause of her thrombocytopenia?
questions.explanation: Drug-dependent immune thrombocytopenia. This woman's profound sudden-onset thrombocytopenia is most likely due to her quinine sulphate therapy, probably given for leg cramps. Drug-related thrombocytopenia can occur due to bone marrow suppression,predictable or idiosyncratic, or by an immune mechanism. Quinine in an idiosyncratic manner causes an immune-mediated profound thrombocytopenia. The patient recovers on withdrawal of the drug but may require steroids in the short term. Thrombocytopenia rours rapidly on re-challenge, including to quinine in tonic water.

questions.question:
298. The hematology registrar is contacted urgently about a woman who has attended an antenatal clinic that morning. She is 32 weeks' pregnant and has a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg and mild proteinuria. Her pregnancy has been complicated by hyperemesis. At booking at 16 weeks' gestation: Her Hb was 11.2 g/dl, MCV 105 f.,MCH 30 pg, MCHC 32 g/dl, WCC 11.3 x 109/L and platelets 237 x 109/L. Now at 32 weeks' gestation her Hb is 5.9 g/dl, MCV 118 fl, MCH 32 pg, MCHC 32 g/dl, WCC 6.4 x 10/L and platelets 154 x 109/L.
What is the most likely cause of her anaemia?
questions.explanation: Folic acid deficiency. This woman, at booking, had a macrocytosis. She is now anemic with profound macrocytosis. This is most likely to be due to folic acid deficiency:humans are just in folic acid balance and pregnancy causes an increased demand. In this case her intake may have been further compromised by emesis. As fertility is reduced in women with a vitamin B12 deficiency, and this condition develops over years, this is lss likely to be the cause. Causes of folic acid deficiency include nutritional (eg old age,poverty, special diets), malabsorption (eg tropical sprue, coeliac disease), exces utilization (eg pregnancy, prematurity, hemolytic anemia, myelofibrosis, malignancy and inflammatory disease), drugs which interfere with metabolism (anticonvulsants,sulfasalazine) and mixed (liver disease, alcoholism, intensive care).

questions.question:
299. A 26-year-old teacher presents to A&E with a rash on her lower legs and a blood blister on her tongue. Her last menses, 2 weeks ago, was heavier than usual. Otherwise she is very well and has no past medical history of note. On examination, there are several small blood blisters on her tongue and a fine petechial rash on her lower legs.There are no other abnormal clinical findings. Her Hb is 12.8 g/dl, with normal indices,WCC 8.6 x 109/L, with a normal differential, and platelets 12 x 109/L.
What would the best immediate management of this patient include?
options: B- Oral prednisolone: 1-2 mg/kg (50-100mg daily dose)
questions.explanation: Oral prednisolone: 1-2 mg/kg (50-100mg daily dose). The most likely diagnosis in this well young woman is immune thrombocytopenic purpura. The patient frequently forms autoantibodies against the platelet glycoprotein lla-IIIb complex. This leads to the removal of platelets from the circulation by the reticuloendothelial system (RES), and their destruction by macrophages in the spleen and throughout the RES. Patients may spontaneously recover from an acute episode, but steroids, splenectomy, intravenous immunoglobulin and immunosuppressive drugs (eg azathioprine and cyclophosphamide)may be required. This woman is well, and therefore should be given steroids as the firstline therapy. Intravenous immunoglobulin and splenectomy are used if steroids fail or the patient relapses. Patients are only given platelets if there is life-threatening bleeding.

questions.question:
300. An 80-year-old women regularly attends the hematology out-patients for her chronic lymphocytic leukemia. She has been followed up for 5 years, her condition has remained stable and she has required no treatment. At this clinic attendance, she reports that she has been feeling extremely tired for the last 2 weeks. On examination she is clinically anemic and mildly jaundiced. She has a 2-cm splenomegaly. There are no other abnormal physical findings. Her Hb is 6.3 g/dl, MCV 103 fl, MCH 29 pg, MCHC 32 g/dl, reticulocytes 205 x 109/L (normal range 50-100), WCC 85 x 109/L, with lymphocytes of 65.5 x 10/L and platelets 110 x 109/L.
What is the main cause of her anemia?
options: B- Progression of chronic lymphocytic Leukemia
C- Iron deficiency due to blood loss
D- Richter's transformation of chronic lymphocytic leukemia
questions.explanation: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia Many patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemid temain in the early stages of the disease and never need any therapy. However, 5-37% of patients can develop autoimmune hemolytic anemia, often late in the disease. Laboratory features of hemolysis include elevated serum bilirubin, elevated LDH, macrocytosis due to reticulocytosis and bone marrow erythroid hyperplasia with the myeloid:erythroid Tatio reduced to 1:1 or reversed. Hemolysis may be provoked by chemotherapy, which may allow the emergence of an antibody-producing clone. It is treated with corticosteroids; if there is no response to steroids then intravenous immunoglobulin ciclosporin and splenectomy may be considered.

questions.question: 301. Which one of the following malignant tumors has the highest predilection for dissemination to bone?
questions.explanation: Prostate Tumors that have a predilection for dissemination to bone are those of the prostate (32%),breast (22%), and kidney (16%) followed by the lung and the thyroid,However, the probability of bone metastasis originating from a primary site can be assessed only by knowing the prevalence of the cancer and its predilection for bone,Therefore, the frequency of bone metastases depends on the prevalence of the cancer in a particular community. Overall frequencies of carcinoma-caused bone metastases for both sexes involve the following areas, in descending order of frequency; breast,prostate, lung, colon, stomach, bladder, uterus, rectum, thyroid and kidney.
